characters.description: A 27-year-old mage and discharged soldier who comes to Fairford to claim a neglected homestead. After ten years of war, he wants the farm to provide a quiet retirement, although his painful mana practice and extraordinary strength mark him as far from an ordinary farmer.
characters.name: John Sutton

characters.description: Fairford's village leader and successor to his late father in the post. He verifies John's deed to the former Burrows homestead while cautioning that the neglected property and the assets listed with it may no longer match the official record.
characters.name: Holden

characters.description: An armed hunter guarding the mountain approach to Fairford. He challenges John on arrival, questioning his identity and purpose before allowing him onward, then directs the newly discharged soldier to Holden, the village leader.
characters.name: George

characters.description: The deceased former owner of the homestead granted to John by deed.
characters.name: Burrows

characters.description: A young caretaker living at the disputed homestead with Ben. When John arrives, Wale and his companions are pressuring her to leave with them on behalf of an unnamed boss.
characters.name: Ellie

characters.description: Ellie’s younger brother and a fellow caretaker living at the disputed homestead. He is there when Wale’s group pressures Ellie to leave with them.
characters.name: Ben

characters.description: Wale commands the men who are trying to make Ellie leave the homestead for an employer whose name is not disclosed. John arrives during the confrontation.
characters.name: Wale

characters.description: A breeding bull included among the cattle listed in John’s deed but missing when he takes possession of the homestead.
characters.name: The bull

characters.description: The Red Coral Adventuring Team's herbalist. She carries a staff, healing supplies, a hand crossbow, and other practical equipment. She presents the experienced group's presence near John's farm as part of a search for a noble family's lost heirloom.
characters.name: Catherine

characters.description: The large and forceful leader of the five-member Red Coral Adventuring Team. He speaks for the armed group when it approaches John's land and claims the team is seeking a noble family's heirloom in an unconfirmed ruined site somewhere in the valley.
characters.name: Reese

characters.description: A ranger with the Red Coral Adventuring Team. Physical contact with John ends in a swift rebuff and convinces him that the new farmer has the strength of a powerful classholder, making John's abilities a subject of concern for the whole team.
characters.name: Grimes

characters.description: A rogue in the Red Coral Adventuring Team. After her companions conclude that John is probably a powerful classholder, she is assigned to watch him while the rest of the group continues its concealed search for a tower in the valley.
characters.name: Sandra

characters.description: The reported leader of Wolf Den, a mountain bandit stronghold at the far end of the valley. He is a titled tamer who specializes in wolves.
characters.name: Haver

characters.description: A huge barbarian classholder aligned with Wale at Wolf Den. His body is reinforced by mana, and Wale summons him as the outpost's principal means of physical intimidation when John arrives alone to reclaim the stolen cattle.
characters.name: Jemal

characters.description: The farm's recovered bull, newly named after showing unusual cunning. Rewards of mana help train him for plowing, while a mana-seeking vine he secretly tends may be increasing his intelligence.
characters.name: Ferdie

characters.description: A historical mage who led a valley tower devoted to magical plant research. His journal describes attacks on the project and the transfer of essential work to the concealed Shadow Tower.
characters.name: Tower Master Kelvis

characters.description: Fairford's innkeeper and a local contact for the regular supply caravans. When John needs equipment that village craftspeople cannot readily provide, Sven explains how to reach the outside merchants who can carry a forge and other farm goods into the valley.
characters.name: Sven

characters.description: A caravan master and merchant who immediately recognizes the identity John is hiding from Fairford. Under John's orders, he agrees to behave as an ordinary supplier, keep that knowledge secret, obtain goods from outside the valley, and explore selling the farm's cheese.
characters.name: Gofreid

characters.description: A swift rogue serving under Haver. She ignores his instruction to remain with the main force, scouts ahead toward Sutton Farm, and attacks John alone with thrown knives and paired curved blades, relying on rapid changes of position.
characters.name: Rosalee

characters.description: At the expedition briefing, Rosalee is identified as the rogue known as the Laughing Blade and as one of the fighters hired alongside Haver and John.
characters.name: Rosalee

characters.description: An unusually large rooster purchased with eleven hens and their coop for Sutton Farm. His formidable claws, aggressive confidence, and defiant response to being handled distinguish him immediately from the rest of the newly acquired flock.
characters.name: Sigvald

characters.description: A dairy farmer trying to leave the valley because of the unresolved killings along its roads. John finds him travelling with 23 neglected cows, and Keller agrees to sell the entire herd for one gold coin per animal if John also helps him depart safely.
characters.name: Keller

characters.description: John's former military adjutant and a skilled duelist with a mana-powered prosthetic arm. He has saved John's life before, recognizes his concealed identity, and accepts work on the farm.
characters.name: Thomas Little

characters.description: A young farmworker recommended through Sven and hired full-time to help milk Sutton Farm's enlarged herd. His arrival adds a regular worker to the household's rotation as dairy production grows beyond what Ellie, John, and Thomas can manage alone.
characters.name: Evan

characters.description: A monk travelling as a member of Reese's Red Coral team on the expedition to the mountain ruins.
characters.name: Red Coral monk

characters.description: One of Haver's bonded wolves. Tag sacrifices his own spirit to heal Haver, who explains that their twin-wolf bond allows Tag to be bonded again eventually.
characters.name: Tag

characters.description: One of Haver's bonded wolves. Haver distinguishes Zeke from Tag by confirming that Zeke is permanently gone.
characters.name: Zeke

characters.description: The noble employer behind Red Coral's tower expedition. Catherine identifies him only after John overtakes her, explaining that Vosik's ancestor secretly retained an extra tower token and that the earl has the means to open the retrieved ornate box.
characters.name: Earl Vosik

recaps.ending: John returns to Sutton Farm after reclaiming the ornate box and tower token from Catherine. Reese and Sandra die fighting Thomas Little, Ferdie, and Sigvald, while Ellie kills Grimes with a curse and survives the resulting mana injury after John intervenes. Haver reaches the farm alive, sees that its defenders have prevailed, and withdraws. The household and dairy remain secure, with Thomas and Evan working alongside John, Ellie, and Ben. Red Coral's assault is ended, but Catherine's fate is unconfirmed and Earl Vosik remains connected to the tower scheme. Ellie learns that her interrupted class ceremony may still permit a future magical class, probably involving water, while Ben is revealed not to be her biological brother. John identifies Tower Master Kelvis as Storm Master Kelvis and opens the recovered box to find six water-magic spell scrolls. Kelvis's testament points toward an undiscovered inverted tower containing his student's research and connects that work to the world-changing summoning. John still must develop food that can withstand mana and prevent his doom total from reaching the apocalypse threshold.
recaps.in_short: John Sutton, a discharged mage seeking retirement, claims a neglected Fairford farm and makes Ellie and Ben part of its household. He recovers stolen cattle, develops a dairy and cheese business, and learns that peaceful human bonds can reduce the doom points that threaten to begin an apocalypse. His crop experiments and recovered mage research point toward food able to survive a mana-altered world. After fighting Haver, John later joins him and Red Coral on a tower expedition. Red Coral betrays them and sends attackers toward Sutton Farm, but John and Haver survive. The farm's defenders kill Reese, Sandra, and Grimes, and Ellie survives using dangerous curse magic. John recovers the expedition's ornate box and discovers water-magic scrolls. He also identifies Tower Master Kelvis as Storm Master Kelvis and learns of an inverted tower holding further research tied to the summoning. The farm is secure, but the apocalypse, Ellie's unfinished magical development, Earl Vosik, and the hidden tower remain unresolved.

recaps.text:
John Sutton arrives in the Robain Mountains after leaving the Royal Lepirian Army, intending to retire on a farm granted to him near Fairford. Village leader Holden confirms the deed but warns that the neglected property is not what its records promise. At the homestead, John finds Ellie and Ben living in poverty while Wale and his men claim the farm's six cows and bull under a supposed debt. John takes possession, allows the siblings to remain as workers, and gives Wale three days to return the livestock.

John also encounters the Red Coral Adventuring Team, whose stated search for an heirloom conceals an interest in a tower. Fairford treats Ellie as a witch, and she implicates Holden in the rumors that isolated her. George directs John to Wolf Den, where Wale serves a bandit leader known as the Wolf King. John goes there alone, defeats the defenders, and returns with every stolen animal. With the cattle restored and Ellie and Ben established in his household, his initial retirement quest is complete. Holden's conduct, Red Coral's surveillance, the Wolf King, and recurring warnings about an approaching apocalypse remain unresolved.

John learns that retirement is only one part of an apocalypse quest. If his doom reaches 100 points, the apocalypse begins, and his next task is to create wheat able to survive any environment. Because mana has ruined farmland elsewhere, he treats the assignment as a possible answer to famine. He starts ordinary plowing with the recovered bull and expands the dairy's storage.

At an abandoned quarry, John trades mana crystals with intelligent grimm for a metal chest and unusual flowers. The chest contains seeds, mage clothing, and a locked journal. John discovers that quiet companionship with Ellie can lower his doom, while destructive magic raises it. The bull grows more intelligent after consuming mana and tending a mana-seeking vine, and John names him Ferdie. Together they build a fortified underground cheese cellar that can shelter Ellie and Ben.

John opens the journal away from the farm. It describes Tower Master Kelvis's old plant-research tower and the hidden Shadow Tower created after repeated attacks. Experiments there produced plants that grow without sunlight and seek mana. The grimm flowers appear connected to that work, giving John and Ellie a possible path toward crops suited to the altered world.

Haver, the Wolf King, arrives with Wale, Jemal, Rosalee, and wolves. He claims the valley, demands the cattle, and orders John to surrender Ellie. John refuses. At the same time, caravan master Gofreid recognizes John's concealed identity and agrees to keep it secret while supplying the farm and marketing its cheese.

When Haver attacks, Rosalee's advance ambush fails. Haver then diverts most of his force toward the farm while Jemal and two wolves hold John back. John kills all three, but the violence increases his doom. Ellie helps him settle the dangerous mana surge afterward. Haver and Rosalee survive, later appearing openly in Fairford, where John bars them from his land and Haver accepts the boundary.

The household adds eleven hens and the formidable rooster Sigvald. Ben takes charge of the chickens, while John and Ellie plan more housing and dairy infrastructure. John's corn trials show the central agricultural problem: heavy mana makes crops grow rapidly, but the plants store it at dangerous levels instead of becoming safe food. The farm is becoming a lasting home for John, Ellie, and Ben, but the mana-resistant food quest and a pattern of murders in the valley remain open.

John buys 23 neglected cows from Keller and escorts the departing farmer safely out of the valley. He also purchases Keller's land, gaining a mountain spring, grazing rights, and a flooded iron mine. After recovering iron and forging pipes, John installs running hot and cold water, sanitation, and expanded dairy facilities. The mana-treated corn remains unsuitable for people, though it can feed animals.

Gofreid formalizes a distribution partnership for Sutton Farm cheese. The enlarged herd creates an urgent labor shortage, leading to the arrival of Thomas Little, John's former military adjutant. Thomas recognizes John's hidden identity, joins the household as a farmhand and defender, and agrees to train Ben. Evan is hired as another milker. With regular milk sales, cheese shipments, a planted wheat crop, and additional staff, Sutton Farm becomes a functioning commercial dairy.

Reese asks John to accompany Red Coral on an expedition to ruins in the mountains because the group has found signs of dangerous beasts. John agrees only to hear the team's proposal.

John departs with Red Coral, Haver, and Rosalee for a ruined academy tower. Rosalee secretly warns John to watch for betrayal. A larger-than-expected gnoll force drives the party through a sealed entrance, leaving the expedition trapped underground and dependent on a lower-level portal for escape. Thorn bears pursue them through the corridors. Tower traps decapitate Rosalee and the Red Coral monk, while John and Haver form a temporary pact after concluding that the local recruits are being used as expendable protection.

In the lowest hall, Catherine retrieves an ornate box that is supposedly needed before the portal can operate. The Red Coral members then attack John and Haver. Haver is poisoned, one of his wolves dies defending him, and the adventurers escape through the portal before destroying it from the far side. Catherine leaves with the box toward the capital, while Reese, Sandra, and Grimes head toward Sutton Farm. Grimes states his intention to take Ellie. John and Haver are stranded with eight thorn bears, and the farm faces an attack without either of them visibly present.

John reveals his full power and kills all eight thorn bears, increasing his apocalypse doom in the process. Haver survives Catherine's poison when his remaining bonded wolf sacrifices its spirit to heal him. The two men recover mage books, documents, a compass-like artifact, a quill, and a Mental Model skill scroll before escaping the tower. They pursue the betrayers, then split up. Haver races after the three adventurers bound for Sutton Farm, while John follows Catherine. He forces her to surrender the ornate box and access token and learns that Earl Vosik commissioned the retrieval. When she attacks again, John severs her leg, but her final fate is not established.

At Sutton Farm, Ellie delays Reese, Sandra, and Grimes until the defenders can act. Thomas Little kills Sandra, while Ferdie and Sigvald defeat Reese. Ellie draws Grimes into the woods, uses tea to bind him to a curse, and fatally stabs him. The mana strain nearly kills her, but John arrives and removes it. Haver sees that the farm has defended itself and leaves. All three attackers sent to the farm are dead, and Ellie's recovery is expected.

After the attack, Ellie explains that her grandmother attempted to transfer a witch class to her. Ellie's different affinity interrupted the ceremony, leaving her with limited mana capacity rather than a completed class. She also reveals that Ben is not her biological brother: she found him in ruins when they were children and later presented them as siblings. John invests all his unused skill points in Mental Model and determines that Ellie may still gain a mana-using class once she finds the right medium, with water the strongest current possibility.

John returns to the grimm exchange and opens recovered mage materials. He confirms that Tower Master Kelvis was also Storm Master Kelvis. Kelvis's testament says he participated in the world-changing summoning and concealed an inverted tower in the mountains, where his student's research remains. The compass and quill were left to help locate it. John also opens the ornate box and finds six water-magic spell scrolls. Sutton Farm ends the book secure and expanding, but John still faces the apocalypse threshold and the unfinished search for mana-compatible food. The inverted tower, Ellie's magical path, Catherine's uncertain fate, and Earl Vosik remain open.

characters.description: A practical Kansas girl already familiar with Oz and its wonders. While traveling in California, she is caught in an earthquake and dropped into a strange country beneath the earth with Zeb, Jim, and Eureka.
characters.name: Dorothy Gale

characters.description: Dorothy's young cousin, who is driving her from the railway station when the earthquake opens beneath them. Though the underground marvels alarm him, he loyally shares the dangers of the journey.
characters.name: Zeb Hugson

characters.description: The farm horse pulling Zeb's buggy. Once below the earth he can speak, but remains a plain, skeptical horse who would prefer dependable oats and solid ground to magic.
characters.name: Jim

characters.description: Dorothy's small white kitten. In the lands beneath the earth she gains speech and shows herself curious, proud, and inclined to chase anything smaller than herself.
characters.name: Eureka

characters.description: Dorothy's old friend, formerly the celebrated ruler of the Emerald City. His balloon descends into the underground country, and his stage tricks and resourcefulness make him valuable to the stranded travelers.
characters.name: The Wizard

characters.description: The handsome young ruler of the Mangaboos, a people who grow like plants in a city of glass. He receives the visitors with suspicion and expects the Wizard to explain the damage caused by his arrival.
characters.name: Prince of the Mangaboos

characters.description: A newly grown ruler of the Mangaboos. Beautiful and cold, she regards ordinary flesh-and-blood people as troublesome strangers and soon makes their position in the glass city dangerous.
characters.name: Princess of the Mangaboos

characters.description: A solitary man living among cliffs, where he braids many kinds of manufactured goods from his long hair. He gives the travelers food and directions during their search for a way upward.
characters.name: The Braided Man

characters.description: The young ruler of Oz and Dorothy's friend. She possesses powerful magic and watches for Dorothy's return from a distance when the underground journey has nearly exhausted every other hope.
characters.name: Ozma

characters.description: Dorothy's old companion, made of straw and famous in Oz for the brains the Wizard once gave him. He welcomes the travelers and is eager to compare his unusual abilities with Jim's ordinary strength.
characters.name: The Scarecrow

characters.description: A lively wooden horse who serves Ozma and her friends. He is small beside Jim but swift, tireless, and confident that an enchanted creature can outdo a farm horse.
characters.name: The Sawhorse

recaps.ending: Ozma brings Dorothy and her companions safely to Oz, where Zeb and Jim meet Dorothy's extraordinary friends. Jim races the Sawhorse and learns that an enchanted wooden horse has advantages an ordinary animal cannot match. Suspicion then falls on Eureka when one of the Wizard's nine tiny piglets disappears. At a formal trial the kitten is found guilty after seeming to admit the deed, but the Wizard produces the missing piglet alive from his coat pocket and clears her. The Wizard chooses to remain in Oz and study real magic under Glinda. Zeb is too homesick for ordinary life to settle in the fairyland, while Jim also longs for his familiar stable. Ozma uses the Magic Belt to send Zeb and Jim back to their California ranch and Dorothy and Eureka home to Kansas. The underground party therefore separates safely, with Dorothy able to visit her friends in Oz again and the Wizard at last becoming one of them.
recaps.in_short: An earthquake in California drops Dorothy, her cousin Zeb, the horse Jim, and the kitten Eureka into a succession of countries beneath the earth. They meet Dorothy's old friend the Wizard, whose balloon has also fallen, and together escape the glass city of the vegetable Mangaboos. Their route passes through a valley of invisible people, a country of wooden Gargoyles, and a cavern of young dragons. When they can go no farther, Ozma magically carries them to Oz. After reunions and contests, Eureka is accused of eating one of the Wizard's tiny piglets, but the animal is found unharmed. The Wizard stays in Oz to learn magic, while Ozma sends homesick Zeb and Jim back to California and returns Dorothy and Eureka to Kansas.

recaps.text: Dorothy Gale has visited the Land of Oz more than once. On her first journey she befriended the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman and exposed the celebrated Wizard as an ordinary showman. On a later visit she met Ozma, the rightful young ruler of Oz, and helped restore the royal family of Ev. Dorothy has since returned to her Kansas home, but Ozma remains her friend.

While visiting relatives in California, Dorothy rides from the railway station with her young cousin Zeb, his horse Jim, and her kitten Eureka. An earthquake opens the road beneath them, and the entire buggy falls into a glowing underground country. Jim and Eureka discover that they can speak there. The travelers reach a city of glass inhabited by the Mangaboos, people who grow on plants rather than being born. A balloon soon descends carrying Dorothy's old friend the Wizard of Oz. The Mangaboos blame the strangers for damage in their city, and the travelers realize that they must find another way home.

Dorothy, Zeb, the Wizard, Jim, and Eureka escape the Mangaboos through a dark passage. They emerge in the Valley of Voe, whose people and dangerous bears are invisible because of a magical fruit. With help from friendly inhabitants, the party crosses the valley without being caught by the bears. A Braided Man living alone among the cliffs supplies food and explains some of the strange lands around them. Still searching for a route toward the surface, the travelers enter a country inhabited by wooden Gargoyles, who attack intruders despite being unable to speak.

The travelers fight their way out of the Gargoyles' country and cross a cavern occupied by young dragons whose larger parents are away. At last they reach a place from which no ordinary escape seems possible. Dorothy calls on Ozma, trusting that her friend may be watching through the Magic Picture. Ozma uses the Magic Belt to bring the whole company to the Emerald City. Dorothy and the Wizard reunite with their Oz friends, while Zeb and Jim marvel at a land where beings such as the Scarecrow and Sawhorse are alive.

In Oz, Jim races the Sawhorse but cannot beat the tireless enchanted creature. A more serious dispute begins when one of the Wizard's nine tiny piglets vanishes and Eureka is accused of eating it. Ozma oversees a trial, and the kitten's own evasive answers make her look guilty. The Wizard finally produces the missing piglet alive from his pocket, proving that Eureka did not eat it. He decides to remain in Oz and learn genuine magic from Glinda. Zeb and Jim prefer their familiar California home, so Ozma sends them back to the ranch with the Magic Belt. Dorothy and Eureka are likewise returned safely to Kansas, ending the adventure with every traveler where he or she most wishes to be.

characters.description: The head of the British Secret Service station in Jamaica. His unexplained disappearance, after he begins investigating a restricted private island, is the event that sends Bond to the colony.
characters.name: John Strangways

characters.description: Strangways's secretary at the Jamaica station. Reliable and punctual, she disappears on the same evening as her chief, leaving the station's routine abruptly broken.
characters.name: Mary Trueblood

characters.description: A British Secret Service officer returning to duty after serious poisoning. He is sent to Jamaica on what his superiors present as a comparatively quiet inquiry into a missing station chief.
characters.name: James Bond

characters.description: The head of the British Secret Service. Concerned that Bond's equipment and judgement contributed to his last injury, he changes Bond's sidearm and assigns him the apparently limited task of resolving the Jamaica disappearances.
characters.name: M

characters.description: A neurologist who oversees Bond's recovery and advises the Service on whether he is fit to resume operational work.
characters.name: Sir James Molony

characters.description: A senior colonial official in Jamaica who assists Bond with records concerning Crab Key. Courteous but uneasy, he knows that official reluctance and missing files have obstructed scrutiny of the island.
characters.name: Pleydell-Smith

characters.description: A wealthy and reclusive owner of Crab Key, where guano is mined under strict private control. He is associated with the disappearance of observers who challenged his activities and with interference affecting nearby American missile tests.
characters.name: Dr Julius No

characters.description: A Cayman Islander, skilled fisherman, and trusted former ally of Bond. His knowledge of Jamaican waters and fieldcraft makes him Bond's essential partner in the secret approach to Crab Key.
characters.name: Quarrel

characters.description: A young Jamaican photographer who takes Bond's picture soon after his arrival. Her interest appears connected to local surveillance rather than routine press work.
characters.name: Annabel Chung

characters.description: A self-reliant young woman who lives by collecting valuable shells and secretly visits Crab Key for better specimens. Largely isolated from conventional society, she knows the shore and its wildlife intimately and refuses to be intimidated by Bond's authority.
characters.name: Honeychile Rider

characters.description: A severe attendant at Dr No's installation who supervises Bond and Honey after their capture, presenting the compound's coercion under the surface manners of a private institution.
characters.name: Sister Lily

recaps.ending: Dr No explains that he is disrupting American missile tests for the Soviet Union and intends to kill his captives through staged ordeals. Bond is forced through a hazardous obstacle route built into the installation and survives a final struggle with a giant squid. Honey, left to be eaten by crabs, escapes because the animals do not attack as Dr No expected. Bond reaches the working area, takes control of a loading machine, and sends Dr No into the flow of guano, where he is buried and killed. Bond reunites with Honey, and they escape Crab Key in the armoured vehicle used to frighten intruders before sailing back toward Jamaica. Bond arranges for the authorities to take control of the island and frames the immediate report to protect the mission's sensitive elements. He and Honey recover together after the operation.
recaps.in_short: After station chief John Strangways and his secretary disappear in Jamaica, Bond is sent to investigate. The trail leads to Crab Key, the private guano island of Dr Julius No, who is suspected of killing intruders and interfering with American missile tests. Bond and his old ally Quarrel land secretly and meet shell collector Honey Rider. Dr No's armoured flame-throwing vehicle kills Quarrel, and Bond and Honey are captured. No reveals that he works with Soviet interests and intends to dispose of them through elaborate ordeals. Bond survives an obstacle course and a fight with a giant squid; Honey escapes a separate attempt on her life. Bond commandeers machinery and buries Dr No in guano, killing him. He and Honey flee the island and return to Jamaica, leaving the authorities to secure the installation.

recaps.text: In Jamaica, station chief John Strangways and his secretary Mary Trueblood are killed and removed by an organised group, leaving their office to appear suddenly abandoned. In London, Bond has recovered from poisoning sustained on his previous mission. M questions his recent judgement, orders him to adopt a different handgun, and sends him to determine what happened in Jamaica. The assignment is presented as a way to return to work without excessive danger. Bond arrives knowing only that Strangways had become interested in Crab Key, a privately owned island whose protected bird colony and guano business discourage visitors.

Bond consults colonial official Pleydell-Smith and discovers missing records and widespread unease around Crab Key's owner, Dr Julius No. Strangways had linked the island to unexplained disruption of American missile trials and to the deaths of bird wardens. Attempts are made to frighten or kill Bond, including a poisoned delivery and a venomous centipede placed in his bed. He recruits his old ally Quarrel, who knows the local sea and has helped Strangways. They train and prepare a secret night crossing to Crab Key, accepting that official channels have been watched or compromised.

Bond and Quarrel reach Crab Key by small boat and conceal their landing. On the beach they meet Honeychile Rider, an independent shell collector who visits the forbidden shore for rare specimens. Bond persuades her that the island's guards are now actively hunting them. The three move inland through marsh and cover while patrols search the coast. Honey's knowledge of the terrain helps them avoid immediate capture, but Dr No's organisation deploys a vehicle disguised as a fantastic creature to terrify trespassers and drive them from hiding.

The disguised vehicle is armoured and equipped with a flame weapon. It kills Quarrel and captures Bond and Honey. They are taken into Dr No's highly organised installation, cleaned, fed, and treated with artificial courtesy while remaining prisoners. The comfort is another means of control, and staff monitor them closely. Bond searches for weaknesses and tries to preserve his strength while Honey resists the institution's intimidation. They are brought before Dr No, who has built a private domain around the island's guano industry and its strategic position near American weapons testing.

Dr No describes his criminal history, his physical injuries, and his work interfering with American guided-missile tests on behalf of Soviet interests. He treats Bond and Honey as subjects for demonstrations of endurance rather than as prisoners who might leave alive. Bond is placed in a constructed obstacle course that exposes him to heat, electrical shocks, dangerous creatures, and exhaustion. He understands that the route is designed both to gather observations and to kill him while satisfying No's curiosity. Honey is taken away for a separate staged death, leaving each unaware whether the other survives.

Bond completes the obstacle course and survives a final underwater struggle with a giant squid. Honey also escapes: the crabs meant to consume her do not behave as Dr No predicted. Bond enters the island's industrial area, takes control of a loading machine, and sends Dr No into the guano flow, where he is buried and killed. He finds Honey, and they use the armoured vehicle to cross the island before escaping by boat. Back within reach of Jamaica, Bond prepares a report and instructions for authorities to secure Crab Key and its communications equipment. Quarrel is dead, but No's operation is destroyed, and Bond and Honey recover together.

characters.description: A young English solicitor sent from London to Transylvania to conclude a property purchase for a foreign nobleman, Count Dracula. Diligent, practical, and newly engaged to be married, he keeps a careful journal of his journey. Arriving at the Count's remote castle in the Carpathians, he slowly realizes that he is not a guest but a prisoner.
characters.name: Jonathan Harker

characters.description: An ancient Transylvanian nobleman who receives Jonathan Harker at his crumbling castle. Tall, pale, and gaunt, with an iron grip, sharp teeth, and hair on his palms, he is a courteous but deeply unsettling host whose strange traits mount: he keeps no servants, appears only after dark, and casts no reflection in a mirror. He questions Harker minutely about England and holds him captive within the castle walls.
characters.name: Count Dracula

characters.description: A capable, warm-hearted young Englishwoman engaged to Jonathan Harker and working as an assistant schoolmistress. Devoted to her fiance and to her close friend Lucy Westenra, she is methodical and resourceful, skilled in shorthand and typewriting, and grows anxious as Jonathan's letters from abroad turn scarce and strange.
characters.name: Mina Murray

characters.description: Mina's beautiful, good-natured friend, a lighthearted young woman who in a single day receives three marriage proposals. She accepts one suitor while remaining fond of all three. Prone to sleepwalking as she was in childhood, she becomes the object of a mysterious nocturnal menace during a stay at the seaside town of Whitby.
characters.name: Lucy Westenra

characters.description: A young doctor who runs a private lunatic asylum and is one of Lucy Westenra's three suitors. Dedicated and scientific, he records his diary on a phonograph and takes a professional interest in a peculiar patient at his asylum. When Lucy accepts another man, he throws himself into his work.
characters.name: Dr John Seward

characters.description: A wealthy young gentleman, heir to a title, who is the suitor Lucy Westenra accepts and to whom she becomes engaged. Steady, generous, and devoted to Lucy, he is a close friend of her two other suitors.
characters.name: Arthur Holmwood

characters.description: A good-humored, adventurous American from Texas, another of Lucy Westenra's three suitors. Frank and brave, he takes his rejection gracefully and remains a loyal friend both to Lucy's chosen fiance and to her circle.
characters.name: Quincey Morris

characters.description: A patient in Dr Seward's asylum, a powerfully built man of unstable mind who keeps and devours living creatures, first flies, then spiders and birds, believing he absorbs their life force. His moods swing between violence and lucidity, and his agitation seems to rise and fall with events he could not ordinarily know.
characters.name: Renfield

characters.description: A brilliant Dutch physician, philosopher, and former teacher of Dr Seward, summoned from Amsterdam when Lucy falls gravely and inexplicably ill. Learned, energetic, and open-minded, he brings both up-to-date medicine and a knowledge of old and obscure lore to a case that baffles conventional doctors.
characters.name: Professor Abraham Van Helsing

characters.description: Lucy Westenra's widowed mother, an ailing woman with a weak heart who is kept ignorant of the true danger to her daughter for fear the shock would kill her. Gentle and well-meaning, she remains close to Lucy through her mysterious illness.
characters.name: Mrs Westenra

characters.description: Three seductive female figures who confront Jonathan Harker in a forbidden part of Dracula's castle. Fair and alluring but with gleaming teeth and cold, predatory intent, they close in on the trapped Harker as prey until the Count violently drives them off, declaring that Harker belongs to him.
characters.name: The women of Dracula's castle

recaps.ending: The hunters chase Dracula back to Transylvania, guided by the psychic bond he forced on Mina, whom Van Helsing hypnotizes to sense the Count's surroundings. Van Helsing destroys the three vampire women in the castle. At sunset the group overtakes the gypsies hauling Dracula's box of earth toward his home and fights through them. Jonathan Harker slashes the Count's throat and Quincey Morris drives his knife into the heart just before dark; Dracula's body dissolves into dust, ending his power, and the mark on Mina's forehead disappears, showing she is cleansed. Quincey Morris, wounded in the final struggle, dies among his friends, glad that their effort has saved Mina. In a closing note set some years later, Mina and Jonathan are happily married with a young son whose names honor the men of the company, especially Quincey. The survivors reflect that the record they kept is a mass of ordinary documents, yet it stands as testimony to what they endured together.
recaps.in_short: English solicitor Jonathan Harker travels to Count Dracula's castle in Transylvania and discovers his host is a vampire who imprisons him and then sets off for England. In England the Count preys on Lucy Westenra, who sickens and dies despite the efforts of Professor Van Helsing and her suitors, and rises as an Un-Dead until the men stake her. Van Helsing unites Lucy's suitors, Dr Seward, Arthur Holmwood, and Quincey Morris, with Harker and his wife Mina to hunt Dracula. They sterilize the boxes of earth he sleeps in, but Dracula attacks Mina and binds her to his mind before fleeing back to Transylvania. Using Mina's hypnotic link to track him, the group pursues him across Europe and overtakes his coffin at sunset near his castle, destroying him just before nightfall. Dracula crumbles to dust and Mina is freed, though Quincey Morris dies of his wounds.

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, a young English solicitor, travels to a remote castle in the Carpathian Mountains to settle a property purchase in England for a nobleman, Count Dracula. The country people he passes react with dread to his destination. At the castle he finds the Count a courteous but deeply strange old man who keeps no servants, appears only at night, and casts no reflection. Harker slowly grasps that he is a prisoner. He is menaced by three seductive vampire women, from whom the Count saves him for his own purposes, and he sees Dracula crawl down the castle wall like a lizard and lie by day in a box of earth. Realizing the Count means to travel to England and fearing for his life, Harker resolves to escape by any means and is left in desperate peril.

The scene shifts to England, where Mina Murray, Harker's fiancee, exchanges letters with her friend Lucy Westenra. Lucy has received and accepted one of three marriage proposals, choosing Arthur Holmwood over the doctor John Seward and the American Quincey Morris. Anxious at Jonathan's long silence, Mina joins Lucy for a holiday at the seaside town of Whitby. There a storm drives a derelict ship ashore with its captain dead at the wheel and a great dog that bounds away into the night. Lucy begins to sleepwalk, and one night Mina finds her outside with a dark shape bending over her; afterward Lucy is pale and marked at the throat. Meanwhile Dr Seward records the disturbing behavior of Renfield, an asylum patient obsessed with devouring living things.

Lucy grows weak and bloodless despite every care, and Seward, baffled, sends for his old teacher, Professor Van Helsing of Amsterdam. Van Helsing recognizes something beyond ordinary medicine and orders repeated blood transfusions from Arthur, Seward, Morris, and himself, and hangs garlic flowers in her room to protect her. Again and again the protections are disturbed and Lucy relapses. A wolf breaks her window one night, and the shock kills her frail mother. Weakened past saving and with strange wounds at her neck, Lucy dies. Van Helsing, who suspects the terrible truth, takes quiet, unexplained precautions around her body.

Newspapers report a strange woman luring small children on Hampstead Heath and leaving them with wounds on the throat. Van Helsing, now certain, leads Seward, Arthur, and Morris to Lucy's tomb and shows them that she has become one of the Un-Dead, rising at night to prey on children. Overcoming their grief and horror, the men do what is needed to release her: they drive a stake through her heart and sever her head, giving her soul rest. Meanwhile Jonathan Harker has survived and married Mina, and when Van Helsing reads Jonathan's journal of the castle, the scattered clues come together and the company grasps that the Count himself has come to London.

The friends unite under Van Helsing to hunt Dracula, and Mina gathers and orders all their records so the enemy can be traced. They learn that the Count has brought many boxes of his native earth to England to sleep in, and they set about finding and sterilizing each one so he cannot rest in them. Renfield, Seward's patient, proves to be under Dracula's sway and, in a moment of clarity, begs to be released; when he tries to resist his master he is fatally attacked. That same night the men break in to find Dracula forcing Mina to drink his blood, binding her to him. She is left marked and unclean, able to sense the vampire's mind but in danger of becoming like him.

With his hiding places nearly all destroyed, Dracula flees England, shipping himself in his last box of earth aboard a vessel bound for the Black Sea and his homeland. Van Helsing turns Mina's dreadful bond to advantage: he hypnotizes her at dawn and dusk, and through her he hears the lapping water and creaking timbers around the sleeping Count, letting the hunters follow his course. The band sets out across Europe in pursuit, racing to overtake him before he can reach the safety of his castle, while Mina, drawn further under the vampire's influence, insists on going with them and makes them promise to destroy her should she be wholly lost.

The pursuers close in on Transylvania. Van Helsing takes Mina toward the castle and destroys the three vampire women within it, while the others intercept the band of gypsies carrying Dracula's box toward his home. As the sun sets on the last day, they overtake the wagon and fight off its guards. Jonathan Harker cuts the Count's throat with a great knife and Quincey Morris drives his blade into the heart; Dracula's body crumbles to dust and the curse is lifted, the scar vanishing from Mina's forehead. Quincey Morris, wounded in the struggle, dies among his friends. Years later, Mina and Jonathan have a son, named in part for Quincey, and the survivors look back on the ordeal they shared and overcame.

characters.description: A heavily marked Rain Wild girl serving as keeper to the blue queen Sintara, now weeks upriver from everything she knew. She climbs and hunts better than anyone in the company, is steadily becoming more scaled and less human, and is discovering that the rules she was raised under, especially the one forbidding the marked to love or breed, have no enforcement out here and no obvious replacement.
characters.name: Thymara

characters.description: The Bingtown scholar who came north to study dragons and stayed to travel with them, keeping the expedition's records. Her marriage to Hest Finbok is a contract she now understands the worth of, and her feelings for Captain Leftrin have become the thing she is trying hardest not to act on.
characters.name: Alise Kincarron Finbok

characters.description: Captain of the liveship barge Tarman and the expedition's practical authority, responsible for feeding and moving dragons, keepers and passengers up a river that eats boats. He is in love with a married woman, at odds with the hunter he was forced to hire, and keeping a secret about how his barge came to be as awake as he is.
characters.name: Leftrin

characters.description: Hest Finbok's secretary, sent upriver as Alise's companion and secretly commissioned to bring back dragon blood and scales for the Chalcedean trade. Fastidious, homesick and increasingly disgusted with himself, he has taken what he came for and now has to live aboard a small boat with the people he stole it from.
characters.name: Sedric Meldar

characters.description: The blue queen dragon who claimed Thymara, imperious, beautiful and unable to fly. She takes her keeper's devotion as tribute, withholds approval as a tool, and is beginning to find the ground intolerable.
characters.name: Sintara

characters.description: The small copper queen, the most damaged dragon of the clutch, slow of speech and dim of memory, whom nobody expected to survive the journey and no keeper wanted.
characters.name: Relpda

characters.description: The expedition's hunter, an old friend of Leftrin's, competent in the wild and unexpectedly patient with people. He notices what others miss, including how badly the Bingtown secretary is coping.
characters.name: Carson

characters.description: The tattooed former slave among the keepers, tending the small green queen Fente. He is Thymara's oldest friend in the company and would like to be more, in a group where nobody has agreed what any of that is allowed to mean.
characters.name: Tats

characters.description: The strangest and most cheerful of the keepers, devoted past all reason to his small red dragon. Where the other keepers ration their effort, he feeds, grooms and exercises Heeby relentlessly, and is generally regarded as a fool for it.
characters.name: Rapskal

characters.description: Rapskal's small scarlet dragon, unremarkable in memory and intellect but the best fed and best exercised animal in the herd, and enormously fond of her keeper.
characters.name: Heeby

characters.description: The oldest and most heavily marked keeper, who has appointed himself the company's lawgiver. He argues that the expedition is a new people with the right to make its own rules about property, leadership and children, and he is increasingly willing to enforce those rules on people who did not vote for them.
characters.name: Greft

characters.description: A keeper girl who has taken the freedoms of the journey further and faster than the rest, and whose choices become the company's first real crisis when the consequences arrive.
characters.name: Jerd

characters.description: The golden dragon whose argument set the whole migration in motion, and the closest thing the herd has to a leader. He is the only one of them who consistently thinks past the next meal, and he holds fragments of memory the others lack.
characters.name: Mercor

characters.description: The youngest of the keepers, Mercor's devoted attendant, small and gentle and largely ignored in the company's quarrels.
characters.name: Sylve

characters.description: Carson's young nephew, brought along as an extra pair of hands and learning to hunt from him.
characters.name: Davvie

characters.description: The hunter Leftrin did not choose and cannot get rid of, who takes a professional interest in dragon parts and none at all in the expedition's success.
characters.name: Jess

recaps.ending: The expedition finds what it was sent for. Beyond a stretch of dry, open country unlike anything in the Rain Wilds, a broad river runs past the ruins of a great Elderling city, and Rapskal, flying above it on Heeby, sees it whole. Kelsingra is real, largely intact, and on the far bank of a river too wide, cold and fast for the dragons and keepers to cross; the company settles instead in a smaller Elderling village on the near side, with stone buildings, remembered voices in the walls and a view of the city they cannot reach. The dragons that survived the journey are hunting for themselves, several are flying, and their keepers have finished becoming something new: scaled, long-lived, no longer Rain Wilders but Elderlings. Greft's attempt to found a new order among them has ended with his death, and the keepers are left to work out their own arrangements about pairing, children and leadership. Alise has left her marriage behind in every way that matters and is openly with Leftrin, who has told her the truth about Tarman. Sedric has confessed what he came upriver to do, been bonded to the copper queen Relpda, changed into an Elderling himself, and found in Carson a life he never planned for. Leftrin will take Tarman back down the river to claim the Traders' payment and bring back supplies, leaving dragons and keepers to hold a city they can only look at, while in Bingtown, Chalced and the Rain Wild councils other people are already deciding what a rediscovered Elderling city and a herd of recovering dragons are worth.
recaps.in_short: The dragons, keepers and Leftrin's barge Tarman push further up the Rain Wild River. A violent flood sweeps Sedric overboard into the acid water, and the copper dragon Relpda saves him; the dragon blood he had stolen and swallowed binds the two of them mind to mind, which destroys his ability to think of dragons as merchandise. When the hunter Jess turns out to be running the same trade and tries to force him into it, the confrontation ends with Jess dead, Sedric's theft exposed, and Alise learning both what her husband is and what Sedric has been to him. Among the keepers, Greft's attempt to found a new society founders on Jerd's pregnancy and on his own hardening authority, and he dies before he can settle it. The dragons begin to hunt and then to fly, Rapskal's small red Heeby first, and the keepers finish changing into Elderlings. Alise and Leftrin become lovers; Sedric and Carson do too. At last the company comes out of the swamp into open country and finds Kelsingra: a vast Elderling city, intact, on the far bank of a river they cannot cross. They settle in a smaller village opposite it, and Leftrin turns Tarman downriver for supplies and payment.

recaps.text: Previously: in the Liveship Traders trilogy, Bingtown's liveships turned out to have been built from stolen dragon cocoons, and the sea serpents trailing them were dragons unable to complete their life cycle. Tintaglia, the last dragon, hatched in the buried Elderling city beneath Trehaug and bargained with the Rain Wilders: she would defend Bingtown against Chalced if they guided the serpents up the Rain Wild River to cocoon. Malta Vestrit and Reyn Khuprus, changed by dragon contact into Elderlings, married; the war ended in a new alliance. But the serpents arrived too late and too few, and in Dragon Keeper the clutch that hatched at Cassarick was stunted: dragons that could not fly or hunt, with fragmentary ancestral memories, dependent on Rain Wilders who resented feeding them. Tintaglia, her bargain kept, went her own way. The Traders' Council paid to make the problem leave: a company of heavily marked young outcasts was hired as keepers, and Captain Leftrin's liveship barge Tarman was contracted to escort dragons and keepers far upriver in search of Kelsingra, an Elderling city the dragons half remember. Among the keepers were Thymara, who should by custom have been left to die at birth and who was claimed by the haughty blue queen Sintara, and the former slave Tats, the odd, fearless Rapskal, the gentle Sylve, and Greft, who intended to lead. Alise Kincarron, a Bingtown dragon scholar in a hollow marriage to the wealthy Hest Finbok, joined the expedition as its recorder, accompanied by Hest's secretary Sedric, who was secretly sent to steal dragon blood and scales for the Chalcedean market and who had begun, at the close of that book, to take them.

A surge of flood water tears down the river, scattering the company and nearly destroying it. Sedric is swept overboard into water that burns, and it is Relpda, the small damaged copper dragon he has been secretly bleeding, who finds him and keeps him alive. The dragon blood he swallowed does what dragon blood does: it opens a bond between them, and Sedric can suddenly hear the creature he had been treating as a supply of raw material. It also begins changing him physically. Whatever he intended to bring back to Bingtown, he can no longer pretend the dragons are animals, and he is now tied to one of them.

The hunter Jess reveals that he is running the same trade as Sedric and for harder masters, and he intends to take a dragon apart properly rather than bleed one discreetly. He tries to force Sedric's cooperation, and the confrontation aboard Tarman ends with Jess dead. Sedric's own theft comes out with it. Leftrin has to decide what to do with a passenger who has been robbing the creatures the expedition exists to protect, and Alise learns two things at once: exactly what her husband arranged, and what Sedric has been to Hest for years. Her marriage stops being a disappointment and becomes a fact she is free to act on.

Cut off from the settlements, the keepers become a society of their own, and Greft intends to write its rules: who leads, who may pair with whom, and whether the Rain Wild ban on the marked having children still binds them. Jerd's pregnancy makes the question immediate rather than theoretical, and the company divides badly over it. Thymara, courted by Tats and complicated by Rapskal, refuses to be assigned to anyone. Aboard the barge, Alise and Leftrin stop pretending, and Leftrin tells her the truth he has kept from everyone: how Tarman came to be more alive than any other barge on the river. Sedric, bonded to Relpda and changing, begins to be useful instead of ornamental.

Food and river both turn against the expedition, and the dragons' survival becomes a matter of whether they can be made to hunt for themselves. Mercor pushes them toward it; the keepers drive, feed and groom them. Rapskal's relentless attention to Heeby pays off first: the small red dragon flies, which nobody expected of the least impressive animal in the herd, and it changes what the others believe is possible for them. The keepers, meanwhile, are visibly no longer Rain Wilders. Scales, altered eyes and lengthening bones mark them all, and the dragons acknowledge without much interest that they are making Elderlings, as their kind always did.

Greft's authority hardens into something the keepers will not accept, and his illness and injuries settle the argument before they can: he dies, and the company is left to work out its own arrangements without him. Jerd's pregnancy ends without a child. The river changes character as the expedition climbs beyond the swamp country, following old Elderling traces, and the dragons take to the air one after another as their strength returns. Thymara, Tats and Rapskal remain tangled with each other and unresolved. Sedric and Carson become a settled pair, and Alise, with no intention of ever going back to Bingtown, records an expedition that has stopped being an errand and become a migration.

The company comes out into dry, open country and finds Kelsingra: a great Elderling city standing largely intact on the far bank of a broad, swift river, seen first from the air by Rapskal on Heeby. It is real, and it is out of reach; dragons and keepers alike cannot cross the water. They settle instead in a smaller Elderling village on the near bank, stone buildings full of remembered voices, and begin to make it habitable. The dragons hunt and fly; the keepers are Elderlings now, long-lived and scaled and no longer anyone's outcasts. Alise is with Leftrin and will not be returning to her husband, and Sedric is bonded, changed and in love. Leftrin turns Tarman back down the river to collect the payment the Traders owe and the supplies the settlement needs, while downstream in Bingtown, Cassarick and Chalced, other people begin working out what a living Elderling city and a herd of recovered dragons might be worth to them.

characters.description: A Rain Wild girl of about sixteen, born so heavily marked that custom required she be left in the forest to die; her father took her back and raised her instead, over her mother's objections. She has black claws instead of nails, scaling across her skin, and no future her people will acknowledge, since the heavily marked are forbidden to marry or bear children. She works the canopy as a gatherer, climbs better than anyone, and has spent her life being told what she is not allowed to want.
characters.name: Thymara

characters.description: A Bingtown Trader's daughter from a family with an old name and no money, plain, freckled and bookish, who taught herself everything known about dragons and Elderlings from copied scrolls. She accepted a marriage offer from a wealthy man she barely knew, on terms that gave her an allowance and the right to pursue her study, and she means to use it.
characters.name: Alise Kincarron Finbok

characters.description: Alise's husband, a rich, handsome and fashionable Bingtown Trader who is charming in company and coldly contemptuous in private. He married for the appearance of a settled life and treats his wife's scholarship as an eccentricity to be tolerated, or used.
characters.name: Hest Finbok

characters.description: Hest's secretary, an elegant and fastidious young man who was Alise's childhood friend before he became her husband's employee. He is sent along to keep Alise company and out of trouble, resents every muddy, insect-ridden mile of the Rain Wilds, and is carrying private arrangements of his own that have nothing to do with her research.
characters.name: Sedric Meldar

characters.description: A large blue queen dragon, hatched malformed and unable to fly, who nonetheless carries herself as the aristocrat she believes she is. She has fragments of ancestral memory, contempt for humans, and an unshakeable conviction that she is owed service. She rejects the name the Rain Wilders gave her and gives her own.
characters.name: Sintara

characters.description: The captain and owner of the liveship barge Tarman, a squat, powerful river man with a rough manner, an unfashionable crew and an unusual attachment to his vessel. He knows the Rain Wild River better than anyone and is guarded about how far up it he has been.
characters.name: Leftrin

characters.description: A golden dragon, the least deformed and by far the most thoughtful of the stunted clutch. Where the others rage or sulk, he plans: it is his argument that the dragons must leave the swamp and go upriver in search of the old Elderling city, and his patience that persuades the humans to help.
characters.name: Mercor

characters.description: The liveship barge, built of wizardwood generations ago in a shape nobody builds any more, with painted eyes and thirty-odd legs he is not supposed to have. He is quieter than any other liveship and much older, and Leftrin is careful about who notices how much of him is awake.
characters.name: Tarman

characters.description: A former slave from Bingtown, tattooed across his face, who came upriver as a boy and has made a place for himself among Rain Wilders who are not sure he counts as one of them. He is steady, practical and one of the few people who has ever treated Thymara as an equal.
characters.name: Tats

characters.description: A cheerfully odd young keeper with scarlet scaling and pale eyes, who says whatever occurs to him and appears to be afraid of nothing at all. The other keepers treat him as a simpleton; his dragon is a small, greedy red queen he insists on calling Heeby.
characters.name: Rapskal

characters.description: A young keeper, small for her age and gentler than most, who attaches herself to the golden dragon Mercor and takes his dignity as her own. She grooms him obsessively and defends him to anyone who calls the dragons vermin.
characters.name: Sylve

characters.description: The oldest and most heavily marked of the keepers, a young man with a hard history who takes it for granted that he will lead. He argues that the expedition is a chance to leave Rain Wild law behind and build something with rules of their own making, starting with the rule that forbids the marked to have children.
characters.name: Greft

characters.description: A keeper girl, blonde and confident, quicker than Thymara to decide that the old prohibitions do not bind them once they are beyond Trehaug's reach.
characters.name: Jerd

characters.description: A small copper-coloured dragon, the weakest and least able of the clutch, half-blind and slow-witted from the damage done to her in the cocoon. Nobody expects her to survive the journey and no keeper wants her.
characters.name: Relpda

characters.description: A hunter hired to feed the expedition, an old friend of Leftrin's, broad and weathered and comfortable in the wild. He is more observant of people than his manner suggests, and he travels with his young nephew Davvie.
characters.name: Carson

characters.description: The second hunter taken on for the journey, a competent enough woodsman whom Leftrin did not choose and does not want aboard. He asks more questions about the dragons than about the game.
characters.name: Jess

recaps.ending: The expedition is committed and well up the Rain Wild River. Fifteen or so heavily marked young keepers, the stunted dragons, Leftrin's barge Tarman, two hired hunters and two Bingtown passengers are strung out along a poisonous river with no map beyond the dragons' unreliable ancestral memories of a city called Kelsingra. Thymara has been claimed by the blue queen Sintara and is learning that a dragon's affection is a form of hunger; the keepers are already changing physically from constant contact with them, growing more scaled and less human. Greft is quietly gathering the younger keepers around the argument that Rain Wild law, including the rule that the marked must never breed, has no force out here. Alise has seen enough of Leftrin's plain competence and enough of her husband's letters to understand what her marriage actually is, and Leftrin, who has troubles of his own concerning how his barge came to be what he is, has fallen in love with her. Sedric, sick of the river and desperate for the money that would buy him a different life, has begun secretly taking from the dragons the blood and scales he was sent to get, which is theft from a sentient being and, if the dragons ever learn of it, a killing matter. Nobody aboard yet knows whether Kelsingra exists, and Trehaug and Cassarick are already discussing how conveniently the whole problem has floated away upriver.
recaps.in_short: Generations after the last dragons vanished, the sea serpents finally return up the Rain Wild River to cocoon, but they come too late and too weak, and what hatches at Cassarick is a clutch of stunted dragons that cannot fly or hunt. The Rain Wild Traders, sick of feeding them, contract a company of heavily marked young outcasts as keepers and pay Captain Leftrin's barge Tarman to escort dragons and keepers upriver in search of the legendary Elderling city of Kelsingra, hoping the whole burden simply disappears. Among the keepers is Thymara, a girl who should have been exposed at birth and who is claimed by the imperious blue queen Sintara. Alise Kincarron, a Bingtown scholar trapped in a hollow marriage to the rich Hest Finbok, comes north to study the dragons and joins the expedition, accompanied by Hest's secretary Sedric, who has his own commission: to steal dragon blood and scales worth a fortune in Chalced. The expedition sets out into unmapped river country, the keepers begin to change into something not quite human, Alise and Leftrin fall in love, and Sedric quietly begins to take what he came for.

recaps.text: Previously, in the Liveship Traders trilogy: the Bingtown Traders' greatest asset was the liveship, a vessel built from wizardwood that woke into life and speech once three generations of its owning family had died aboard. The Vestrit family's ship Vivacia quickened for Althea Vestrit's father and was left instead to her brother-in-law Kyle Haven, setting off a long fight for the ship that dragged in the pirate Kennit, who took Vivacia and used her to make himself king of the Pirate Isles. Meanwhile Chalced made war on Bingtown, and Malta Vestrit and Reyn Khuprus of the Rain Wilds were caught up in what lay buried beneath the Rain Wild city of Trehaug: an entombed Elderling city and, in it, a chamber of dragon cocoons. Wizardwood was never wood. Every liveship had been built from the stolen cocoons of unhatched dragons, and the sea serpents that trailed the ships were dragons in an earlier stage of life, unable to complete it because they could no longer find their way up the Rain Wild River to cocoon and hatch. Tintaglia, the last dragon, hatched from the last intact cocoon, and in exchange for the Rain Wilders' help in guiding the serpents home she agreed to defend Bingtown from the Chalcedeans. The war ended in an alliance between Bingtown, the Rain Wilds, the Pirate Isles and the Three Ships folk. Kennit died; Malta and Reyn, transformed by long exposure to dragon influence into Elderlings, married; and the serpents, escorted at last, went up the river to spin their cocoons near Cassarick. It should have been the return of dragons to the world. Instead the serpents arrived old, exhausted and too few, and the memories they needed to shape themselves properly were largely lost.

The cocooned serpents hatch at Cassarick into a clutch of malformed, undersized dragons. They cannot fly, most cannot hunt, and their inherited memories are patchy and unreliable. Tintaglia, having got what she wanted from the bargain, is rarely seen. The Rain Wild Traders are left feeding a herd of enormous, arrogant, half-crippled creatures that eat everything the settlements can catch and give nothing back. In Trehaug, Thymara lives on the margins of that society: born so heavily marked that custom demanded she be left in the forest, saved by her father and resented by her mother, forbidden by Rain Wild law ever to marry or have children because of what she might pass on. She works the canopy as a gatherer and expects nothing else.

In Bingtown, Alise Kincarron has spent years assembling everything known about dragons and Elderlings from copied Trader scrolls. Plain and unmarriageable, she accepted a proposal from the wealthy Hest Finbok on contract terms that fund her study and permit her to travel, and discovered afterwards what her husband is like when the door closes. She uses the contract to go north to the Rain Wilds to see living dragons, and Hest sends his secretary Sedric with her, an old friend of hers who despises the journey and has motives he does not share. The Rain Wild Traders' Council, meanwhile, has hit on a solution to the dragon problem: pay them to leave. The dragons speak of an Elderling city called Kelsingra somewhere far upriver, and the Council will fund an expedition to find it.

The Council recruits keepers from among the heavily marked young of Trehaug and Cassarick, the ones their families are quietly glad to see go: Thymara, the tattooed former slave Tats, the strange and fearless Rapskal, the gentle Sylve, the ambitious Greft, Jerd and a dozen more. Each is claimed by a dragon, Thymara by the haughty blue queen Sintara. Captain Leftrin's barge Tarman is contracted to carry supplies and to shepherd the party, with the hunters Carson and Jess to feed it. Alise arrives at Cassarick expecting wonders and finds instead a herd of damaged, filthy, magnificent animals whose condition appalls her; she talks her way onto the expedition as its scholar and recorder. Leftrin, gruff and unpolished, is immediately taken with her.

The expedition starts upriver into country no living Rain Wilder has mapped. The dragons are proud, difficult and constantly hungry; the keepers learn quickly that tending them is closer to serving a court than herding livestock, and that a dragon's glamour can bend a human's judgement without the human noticing. Freed of their families and of Trehaug's rules, the young keepers begin sorting themselves out, with Greft arguing that the old law forbidding the marked to breed has no authority beyond the settlements. Aboard Tarman, Alise records everything, and the contrast between Leftrin's plain decency and the marriage she left behind becomes impossible for her to ignore. Sedric, meanwhile, is miserable, filthy, and increasingly desperate.

Sedric's real errand comes clear: dragon parts, blood, scales and organs, are worth an enormous amount in Chalced, where the aging Duke is said to be dying and will pay anything for a cure, and Hest has arranged for Sedric to bring some back. Sedric tells himself it is the price of a life he and Hest could have elsewhere. The river grows more dangerous, the dragons' tempers shorten as food runs thin, and the hunter Jess takes more interest in the dragons than in game. Among the keepers, the physical changes accelerate; constant contact with dragons is remaking them, and nobody knows where that ends. Thymara and Sintara circle each other in a bond that is equal parts devotion and exploitation.

The expedition is committed, far up an unmapped and corrosive river, with no proof that Kelsingra exists at all beyond the dragons' broken ancestral memories. Alise has accepted what her marriage is worth and what Leftrin means to her; Leftrin has fallen in love with her and is keeping his own secrets about the barge he sails. The keepers are visibly less human than when they left, Greft's faction is hardening, and the dragons' hunger is outpacing what two hunters can supply. Sedric, sickened by the river and by himself, begins secretly taking blood and scales from the weakest dragon, an act that is theft from a thinking being and would be a death sentence if the dragons discovered it. Downriver, the Traders congratulate themselves on how neatly the problem has floated away.

characters.description: An apprentice of the Harper Hall, small for his age, endlessly curious and famous throughout Pern for a treble voice that has carried the solo part in every major work the Hall performs. He is also an incurable gambler, trader and collector of other people's business, which has made him as many enemies among the apprentices as his voice has admirers. He assumes his future is settled by his singing, and has never seriously considered what he would be without it.
characters.name: Piemur

characters.description: The Masterharper of Pern, head of a craft with a harper posted in every hold, which makes him Pern's teacher and, quietly, the best-informed man on the planet. He is unusually willing to see what an awkward, over-clever apprentice might be good for, and he does not always explain his reasons in advance.
characters.name: Robinton

characters.description: A journeywoman of the Harper Craft, the first woman to hold the rank, and the composer of songs sung all over Pern. She is bonded to nine fire lizards and is the recognized authority on them. She has been Piemur's friend since she arrived at the Hall as an apprentice, and is one of the few people who takes his troubles seriously.
characters.name: Menolly

characters.description: A journeyman harper who travels constantly on the Masterharper's business, quiet and easily overlooked, which is exactly what makes him useful. He handles the errands that require a harper to be somewhere without being noticed, and increasingly takes Piemur with him.
characters.name: Sebell

characters.description: Headwoman of the Harper Hall, who runs its kitchens, stores and lodgings and keeps track of every apprentice in it. Practical and hard to deceive, she has a soft spot for Piemur that she declines to admit to.
characters.name: Silvina

characters.description: Masterdrummer of the Harper Hall, who runs the drumheights at the top of the Hall's tower. Pern's long-distance messages are beaten out in drum code from height to height across the continent, and he is responsible for every one of them; taciturn, exacting, and interested only in whether a message is sent correctly.
characters.name: Olodkey

characters.description: Lord Holder of Nabol, who took the hold after the conqueror Fax's death and has run it badly and spitefully ever since. Long an obstruction to Benden Weyr and to the Harper Craft, he is now seriously ill, and Nabol has no clear successor.
characters.name: Meron

characters.description: The gold queen fire lizard that hatches from an egg Piemur comes away with, and bonds to him. Fire lizards are small telepathic cousins of Pern's dragons; a queen is the rarest of them, and she becomes Piemur's companion, hunter and, eventually, his only means of sending word to anyone.
characters.name: Farli

characters.description: An orphaned runnerbeast foal that Piemur finds and raises in the Southern Continent, named for his opinion of its intelligence. It follows him across a great deal of unexplored country and turns out to be better company than the name suggests.
characters.name: Stupid

characters.description: Holder of Southern Hold on the far continent, running a growing settlement of northerners on land nobody has ever surveyed. Energetic and shrewd, he is expanding his holding a good deal faster than the northern Lords realize.
characters.name: Toric

characters.description: The young Lord Holder of Ruatha, who is also, uniquely on Pern, a dragonrider. He is not supposed to be in the Southern Continent at all.
characters.name: Jaxom

characters.description: Jaxom's dragon: white, about half the size of an ordinary dragon, and unmistakable to anyone who sees him. No other dragon on Pern looks remotely like him.
characters.name: Ruth

recaps.ending: Piemur is found alive in the Southern Continent by Menolly, Sebell and the Masterharper, after months in which the Harper Hall had no idea whether he had survived. He comes back with a queen fire lizard, a half-tame runnerbeast, an eyewitness account of what the exiled riders and their northern trading partners have been doing, and, most valuable of all, first-hand knowledge of an enormous stretch of country no northerner has ever seen. Instead of being returned to the drumheights or to the Hall's classrooms, he is given the south: the Harper Craft needs the continent explored and mapped, and he is the only person who has done it. The loss of his treble voice, which began the book as the end of his career, turns out to have redirected it rather than finished it, and his standing in the craft now rests on what he can do rather than on how he sounds. Along the way he works out that Sebell is in love with Menolly. Left open are Lord Meron's disputed succession at Nabol, the exiled riders in the south, Toric's quietly expanding hold, and the fact that Piemur has seen a white dragon in the Southern Continent and cannot yet explain it to anyone.
recaps.in_short: Piemur's celebrated treble voice breaks, ending the only future he had ever expected, and the Masterharper reassigns him to learn the drum code in the Harper Hall's drum tower, where the other apprentices resent him and one of them puts him out of action. The posting is partly cover: Robinton and the journeyman Sebell have been using Piemur, who is small, quick and unremarkable, for errands that need a harper nobody notices. Sent to Nabol while its Lord Holder Meron is dying, he comes away with a fire-lizard egg that hatches into a queen he names Farli. Travelling south concealed among trade goods to observe the traffic between certain northern holders and the riders exiled to the Southern Continent, he is left behind and stranded. He survives alone for months, raising an orphaned runnerbeast, exploring a vast tract of unmapped country and observing the exiles, including a glimpse of a white dragon that should not be there. When the harpers finally find him, he is given the south to explore and map, his career redirected rather than ended.

recaps.text: Pern's people shelter in stone holds from Thread, a spore that falls from a neighbouring planet and devours anything living; dragons and their bonded riders burn it from the sky. The Harper Craft reaches everywhere: harpers are posted in every hold, their teaching ballads carry Pern's law and history, and long-distance messages are beaten out in drum code from tower to tower, which makes the Masterharper the best-informed man alive. In Dragonsong, Menolly, a sea holder's daughter forbidden her music, ran away, sheltered from Threadfall in a cliff cave and Impressed nine fire lizards, small telepathic cousins of the dragons that nobody had known could be bonded. Rescued by a dragonrider, she was found at Benden Weyr by the Masterharper, who identified her as the author of songs already being sung across Pern and took her to the Harper Hall. In Dragonsinger she survived a week of hostile examination there and was made the craft's first journeywoman. Among the apprentices who befriended her was Piemur, a small, sharp, endlessly inquisitive boy whose treble voice had carried the solo part in every important work the Hall performed, and who assumed his voice was his whole future. Elsewhere, the riders who could not accept the modern world have been exiled to the Southern Continent, and some northern holders trade with them illicitly.

Piemur's voice breaks in the middle of a rehearsal, and with it goes the career everyone including Piemur had assumed was settled. A boy with no voice, no obvious craft aptitude and a reputation for gambling and knowing everybody's business is an awkward thing for the Harper Hall to place. The Masterharper's answer is to send him up to the drumheights to learn the drum code under Masterdrummer Olodkey. The drum apprentices, who have spent Turns resenting the Hall's celebrated soloist, are not pleased to have him among them, and Piemur arrives at the top of the tower without a friend in it.

Piemur learns the drum measures far faster than the apprentices who have been at them for Turns, which makes his position in the drumheights worse rather than better. The resentment turns physical, he is hurt, and the Masterharper deals with it in his own way. It also becomes clear that the posting was never only about drums: Robinton and the journeyman Sebell have been quietly using Piemur for errands that require somebody small, quick and beneath notice, and the drum tower is a convenient place to keep him between them. Their present concern is Nabol, whose Lord Holder Meron has obstructed Benden and the crafts for Turns, is now dying, and has left the hold's succession unsettled. Nabol has also been trading with people it should not, and the harpers want to know exactly what is moving and where it is going.

Piemur goes to Nabol with the harpers while Meron is dying, and in the confusion around the hold he comes away with a fire-lizard egg. It hatches into a gold queen, which is the rarest kind, and he names her Farli; she bonds to him completely and proves an immediate practical asset, since a fire lizard can carry a message where a boy cannot go. Meron's death leaves Nabol without an agreed heir and a good many people with an interest in the outcome, and it confirms what the harpers suspected about who has been trading with the riders exiled to the Southern Continent. Piemur, who is now both useful and unrecognizable as the Hall's former soloist, is the obvious person to send after the traffic itself.

Piemur travels south hidden among trade goods, intending to see for himself what is being exchanged with the exiled riders, and is left behind when the party goes back north.
