He is stranded on a continent nobody has mapped, with no way to send word, and going near the exiles or the northern settlement would give him away. So he walks. Over the following months he lives off the country with Farli hunting for him, raises an orphaned runnerbeast foal he names Stupid for its intelligence, and crosses an enormous stretch of land no northerner has ever seen: rivers, grass plains and forest running far beyond anything the maps admit exists. He keeps clear of the exiles while watching what they do, and the Harper Hall, hearing nothing, has to assume he is dead.

Piemur eventually works his way back toward the settled coast, where Toric's Southern Hold is expanding into land the northern Lords do not know about, and where the exiled riders are doing something Piemur is close enough to witness. Among what he sees is a white dragon, about half the size of a proper one, which he can identify but not explain. Then the harpers find him: Sebell, Menolly and the Masterharper come south and discover the apprentice they had given up for lost, alive, tanned, bonded to a queen fire lizard and trailing a runnerbeast. What he knows about the exiles and their trade is valuable; what he knows about the Southern Continent itself is far more so, because he has been where no map goes. Rather than being sent back to the drumheights, he is given the south to explore and chart for the Harper Craft. The broken voice that ended his career at the start of the book has redirected it instead, and his place in the craft now rests on what he can do. He also finally understands why Sebell always finds reasons to be near Menolly.

characters.description: The last surviving member of Ruatha Hold's ruling Bloodline. Ten Turns earlier the conqueror Fax slaughtered her family and seized the hold; she survived by hiding among the kitchen drudges, filthy and unremarked, and has spent the years since quietly ruining Ruatha's prosperity so that Fax gains nothing by holding it. Small, fierce and patient, she has an unusual talent for touching and nudging the minds of animals and, to a degree, of people, though she does not understand it and uses it sparingly. She wants Fax dead and Ruatha restored to her line, and she has waited a long time for the chance.
characters.name: Lessa

characters.description: Bronze rider of Mnementh and a wingleader of Benden Weyr, the only dragonweyr on Pern still occupied. Where most riders and holders treat the ancient Threadfall as a story, F'lar has read the Weyr's oldest Records and is convinced the deadly spore is about to fall again after four hundred Turns of quiet. Cool, controlled and out of favour with the Weyr's complacent leadership, he rides out on Search for a girl fit to Impress the queen dragon's next clutch, and treats that Search as the first move in a much longer plan.
characters.name: F'lar

characters.description: F'lar's great bronze dragon, the largest at Benden Weyr. Dragons are telepathic and speak mind to mind with their own riders; Mnementh is placid, dryly amused and unusually willing to notice things his rider misses.
characters.name: Mnementh

characters.description: A conqueror who styles himself Lord of the High Reaches, having taken seven holds by force, among them Ruatha, whose ruling family he had killed. Brutal, vain and openly contemptuous of dragonriders, whom he regards as a useless relic living off the holds' tithes. He attaches himself to the Search party out of suspicion rather than courtesy.
characters.name: Fax

characters.description: Brown rider of Canth and F'lar's half-brother, his wingsecond and the person he trusts most. Easier-tempered and more approachable than F'lar, he handles much of the practical work of the Search and of the Weyr, and he shares his half-brother's conviction that Thread is coming back.
characters.name: F'nor

characters.description: A weaver at Ruatha, taciturn and weighed down by grief: he was once a dragonrider, and his dragon died. Riders who lose their dragons rarely survive the loss; Lytol did, and lives with it. He knows the Weyr's ways from the inside and speaks plainly about what Fax's rule has done to Ruatha.
characters.name: Lytol

characters.description: Fax's principal lady, worn down by repeated childbearing and far into a difficult pregnancy when her husband drags his household to Ruatha. The dragonriders treat her with courtesy and pity; Fax treats her with indifference.
characters.name: Lady Gemma

characters.description: An infant born at Ruatha Hold and orphaned at birth, installed as its Lord Holder with a warder appointed to govern in his name until he comes of age.
characters.name: Jaxom

characters.description: The golden queen dragon hatched at Benden Weyr, and the only queen on Pern once the previous one has died. Queens are the largest dragons and the only ones that lay eggs, so the survival of the species rests on her alone. She grows at an alarming rate and proves as strong-willed as the woman she chooses.
characters.name: Ramoth

characters.description: A senior bronze rider of Benden Weyr and its established leader, comfortable with the long quiet and hostile to change. He regards F'lar's warnings about Thread as dangerous nonsense, and takes charge of instructing the new queen's rider along strictly traditional lines.
characters.name: R'gul

characters.description: Headwoman of Benden Weyr's lower caverns, who runs the Weyr's domestic life and its people with quiet authority. She is F'nor's mother, and among the first at the Weyr to treat its new Weyrwoman with straightforward kindness rather than suspicion.
characters.name: Manora

characters.description: One of the young women brought to Benden Weyr on Search, ambitious and frankly interested in the standing that a dragon and a bronze rider's attention could bring her.
characters.name: Kylara

characters.description: The Masterharper of Pern, head of the craft that carries teaching songs and ballads to every hold, which makes him one of the few people whose word travels everywhere. Shrewd, sociable and a keen judge of politics, he takes the dragonriders' warnings seriously when the Lord Holders will not, and he knows the oldest songs better than anyone alive.
characters.name: Robinton

recaps.ending: Lessa rides Ramoth four hundred Turns into the past, using an ancient Ruathan tapestry as her reference point, and survives a crossing long enough to nearly kill them both. In the past she finds the five Weyrs at full strength at the close of a Pass, facing four hundred Turns with nothing left to fight, and convinces their leaders to bring every dragon and rider forward. They arrive at Benden as an army: enough dragons to cover all of Pern for the whole of the new Pass. F'lar is confirmed as the leader who was right about Thread and who now commands a force capable of fighting it, and Lessa's gamble closes the loop that made the old riddle-song a question in the first place. The holds' contempt for the Weyrs is broken by the plain demonstration that the riders are all that stands between Pern and the spore. What is left unresolved is what Pern will do with several thousand riders displaced from four centuries in its own past, who expect the customs, the authority and the deference of their own time and have arrived in a world that changed without them.
recaps.in_short: On Pern, a long-isolated world, the deadly spore called Thread falls from a neighbouring planet whenever its wandering orbit brings it close, and the only defence is dragons and their bonded riders. After four hundred Turns without a Fall, five of the six Weyrs stand empty and the holds despise the riders they are obliged to support. Convinced Thread is about to return, the Benden bronze rider F'lar searches for a new queen's rider and finds Lessa, the last heir of Ruatha Hold, hiding as a drudge under the conqueror Fax. F'lar kills Fax, Lessa Impresses the queen Ramoth, and when Ramoth flies to mate F'lar becomes Weyrleader. Thread returns as he predicted, and Benden's two hundred dragons cannot cover a planet. After the riders discover that dragons can travel in time as well as in space, Lessa works out from an old riddle-song that the five missing Weyrs went forward in time, rides Ramoth four hundred Turns into the past and persuades them to come. Pern gains the dragons it needs, and with them thousands of riders out of its own distant past.

recaps.text: Pern, a world settled long ago and largely cut off from its origins, is periodically scoured by Thread, a spore that falls from a wandering neighbouring planet and devours anything living it touches. The defence is dragons, bred from a native species, telepathically bonded for life to their riders and able to chew a mineral that lets them flame Thread out of the sky. But Thread has not fallen for four hundred Turns. Five of Pern's six Weyrs stand empty and abandoned, only Benden is still occupied and it is badly undermanned; the holds resent the tithes they pay and treat the riders as parasites on a danger nobody living has seen. F'lar, a Benden bronze rider, believes from the oldest Records that Thread is about to fall again, and rides out on Search for a woman fit to Impress the queen dragon's next clutch. The Search brings him to Ruatha Hold, ruined and sullen under the conqueror Fax, who took it ten Turns ago by killing its ruling family. What nobody knows is that one Ruathan survived: Lessa, hiding as a kitchen drudge, gifted with a strange ability to touch minds, and quietly working to make Ruatha worthless to the man who stole it.

F'lar provokes Fax into a duel and kills him, and Lessa steps out of her disguise to claim Ruatha as its last surviving heir. Fax's exhausted wife, Lady Gemma, dies bearing a son at Ruatha; the infant, Jaxom, is named Lord Holder in his father's place, with the former dragonrider Lytol installed as warder to raise him and govern the hold. Lessa gives up her claim to Ruatha in exchange for a larger one: F'lar takes her to Benden Weyr as a candidate, and on the Hatching Ground she Impresses the golden queen Ramoth, the only queen dragon left on Pern, which makes her Weyrwoman of the last inhabited Weyr. She is furious to discover how much of her new life she is expected to accept without explanation, and how little the Weyr's leadership intends to tell her about why they came looking for her at all.

Lessa chafes under the instruction of R'gul, the Weyr's traditionalist leader, who forbids her to fly Ramoth or to read the Records for herself; she does both anyway. Ramoth grows enormously and comes of age, and when she rises to mate Mnementh outflies every other bronze, which by Weyr custom makes F'lar Weyrleader and finally gives him the authority he has wanted. He drives Benden's riders back into fighting drills nobody has needed for four hundred Turns, over the objections of men who think Thread is a story told to justify the tithe. Lessa, meanwhile, reads. The Records are damaged and full of gaps, but between them and the old teaching ballads one thing becomes clear: the ancient defence assumed six full Weyrs, and Benden has roughly two hundred dragons where thousands are needed. Ramoth's first clutch, unusually large, is the only good news anyone has.

Thread falls. The wandering planet's approach is confirmed and the first Fall drops over Nerat, burning into forest and living flesh exactly as the old songs describe. Benden's riders fight it and win, but the victory exposes the arithmetic: one understrength Weyr cannot cover a whole planet, and Falls will come every few days across every region for fifty Turns. Riders and dragons are scored and injured, and the holds, panicking, discover that the tithe they resented bought the only thing standing between them and being eaten alive. Then an accident reveals something the Weyr had forgotten: a dragon given a place and a time to visualize can travel to both, arriving before it left. Dragons can go between times as well as between places, which lets Benden's small force be in two places at once, but it exacts a heavy toll of exhaustion and disorientation on riders and dragons alike, and a rider who miscalculates simply never arrives.

Time travel buys Benden breathing room and nothing more; the riders are wearing out under a burden meant for six Weyrs. F'nor and Kylara take a group of dragons, candidates and eggs ten Turns into the past to the long-empty Southern Weyr, where they can breed and train a fresh fighting force and return after only months of the present's time. Even that will not be enough. Lessa keeps returning to a fragment of an old teaching song about the Weyrs going away, which no harper can explain; Robinton, the Masterharper, agrees it is a question nobody has ever answered. Setting the song beside the Records' abrupt four-hundred-Turn silence, Lessa reaches a conclusion nobody else has considered: the five Weyrs did not die out, they left, and they may still be reachable. To go to them she needs a place and a time she can hold clearly in her mind, and she finds it in an ancient tapestry at Ruatha, which shows the hold as it looked four hundred Turns ago.

Lessa makes the jump alone on Ramoth, using the tapestry as her reference, and nearly dies doing it: four hundred Turns is far beyond anything a dragon has attempted, and the crossing is long, cold and blank. She arrives in the past, where the five Weyrs are full and a Pass has just ended, leaving thousands of dragons and riders with nothing to fight for four centuries. She persuades their leaders that the future needs them, and the five Weyrs come forward through time to Benden, arriving in the present as a fighting force large enough to defend all of Pern. Pern is saved, F'lar has the dragons he needed, and the riddle-song is answered by the very act of answering it. The cost is not yet obvious: Pern now holds thousands of riders raised four hundred Turns in its own past, accustomed to their own customs and to a deference the modern holds and crafts no longer offer.

characters.description: A former combat nurse, now a physician in her late forties, who returns to Inverness in 1968 with her grown daughter, two years after her husband Frank's death. Twenty years earlier she vanished for three years and came back with a story nobody would believe. Blunt, capable, and long practised at keeping her own counsel, she has come north to learn the fate of the Highland men she left behind in 1746, and to finally tell her daughter the truth about where she was.
characters.name: Claire Randall

characters.description: Claire's twenty-year-old daughter, raised in Boston and now a student, tall and strikingly red-haired. Practical and stubborn like her mother, she is grieving the father who brought her up and is bewildered by her mother's sudden determination to dig through Scottish records for a group of men dead two centuries.
characters.name: Brianna Randall

characters.description: A young Oxford historian, adopted son of the late Reverend Reginald Wakefield of Inverness, who is clearing out the manse after his guardian's funeral when Claire and her daughter arrive. Dark-haired, even-tempered, and a fine singer, he has a scholar's appetite for old papers and agrees to trace what became of a company of Highlanders after the rising of 1745.
characters.name: Roger Wakefield

characters.description: Claire's husband, a Cambridge historian who died two years before her 1968 return to Scotland. His lifelong research into his own eighteenth-century ancestry shadowed their marriage, and he and Claire built a careful life in Boston around a subject they did not discuss.
characters.name: Frank Randall

characters.description: A young Highland laird living in exile in France in 1744, tall and red-haired, still carrying the scars of what was done to him in Scotland. Married to Claire and outlawed at home, he works in his cousin's wine business in Paris while the two of them try to head off the Jacobite rising they know will end in disaster. Shrewd, stubborn, and better educated than his rough life suggests, he is uneasy at scheming against a cause many of his own kin hold sacred.
characters.name: Jamie Fraser

characters.description: Jamie's godfather, a small, weathered, and famously taciturn Highlander who has followed him into exile. Loyal past all argument and dangerous when roused, he serves as bodyguard, messenger, and blunt conscience to the household in France.
characters.name: Murtagh Fraser

characters.description: Jamie's older cousin, a Scottish wine merchant long established in Paris, prosperous, shrewd, and quietly sympathetic to the exiled Stuarts. He hands his house and much of his business over to Jamie while he travels, which gives the couple both money and a foothold in the city's political circles.
characters.name: Jared Fraser

characters.description: A wealthy French nobleman and wine importer whose ship Claire condemns as carrying smallpox, costing him an entire cargo. Elegant, vain, and vengeful, he is rumoured to keep company with people who dabble in the occult, and he treats the loss as a personal insult to be repaid.
characters.name: The Comte St. Germain

characters.description: The exiled Stuart heir, a personable, devout, and impulsive young man convinced that God and his own birthright will restore his father to the British throne. He is chronically short of money and long on confidence, and he seeks out Jamie as a Highlander who might help him raise both funds and men.
characters.name: Charles Stuart

characters.description: A small French street orphan and gifted pickpocket, taken out of a brothel by Jamie and set to lifting and copying private correspondence. Cheerful, quick, and fiercely attached to the man who took him in, he becomes a fixture of the household.
characters.name: Fergus

characters.description: A squat, odd-looking Paris apothecary whose crowded shop sells herbs, charms, and curiosities to duchesses and cutpurses alike. He knows a great deal more about medicine, poisons, and Claire herself than he readily explains, and he becomes her supplier, her teacher, and something close to a friend.
characters.name: Master Raymond

characters.description: The formidable nun who runs L'Hopital des Anges, a Paris charity hospital, with absolute authority and no patience for squeamishness. A trained musician of some reputation before she took orders, she is accompanied everywhere by a large dog and quickly recognises that the English lady volunteering on her wards has real skill.
characters.name: Mother Hildegarde

characters.description: A timid, sheltered English girl of fifteen brought to Paris by her uncle and betrothed against her wishes to a much older French nobleman. Claire recognises her name from a family tree she once studied and takes an interest in her that she cannot explain to anyone.
characters.name: Mary Hawkins

characters.description: A gentle, scholarly young Englishman in poor health, employed as secretary to an English duke visiting France. He is the younger brother of Jonathan Randall, and as unlike him as a man can be; his presence is the first proof Claire and Jamie have that the captain they believed dead is alive.
characters.name: Alexander Randall

characters.description: The English dragoon captain who tortured Jamie at Wentworth Prison and hunted Claire in the Highlands, alive after all and serving in France on his patron's business. Cold, controlled, and predatory, he is the one man Jamie has sworn to kill, and the one man Claire has reason to need kept alive.
characters.name: Jonathan Randall

characters.description: A rich, genial English nobleman with estates on both sides of the border, a taste for young men, and a habit of promising support to whichever cause looks likeliest to win. Jamie has dealt with him before and trusts nothing he says.
characters.name: The Duke of Sandringham

characters.description: War chief of clan MacKenzie and one of the most committed Jacobites in the Highlands, forceful, charming, and openly hungry for the fight he has spent years preparing. He greets the rising as the moment he has waited his whole life for, and he does not care to hear that it might fail.
characters.name: Dougal MacKenzie

recaps.ending: On the eve of Culloden, Jamie and Claire make a last attempt to stop the battle by poisoning Charles Stuart. Dougal MacKenzie overhears them, accuses Claire of witchcraft and treason, and attacks her; Jamie kills him and leaves the body hidden. With the army about to be destroyed, Jamie writes a deed transferring Lallybroch to his nephew and sends Murtagh to see the paper safe. He then takes Claire to Craigh na Dun. She is pregnant again, and he refuses to let the child be born on a battlefield. He tells her he intends to see the Lallybroch men off the field and then die in the fighting, and he asks her to name the child for his father. Claire goes through the stones and returns to 1948 and to Frank, who agrees to raise the child as his own. In 1968 the story catches up with itself: Roger's research turns up a record showing that James Fraser was not killed at Culloden after all. Claire, Brianna and Roger are left with the knowledge that Jamie survived the battle, and that the twenty years since could be crossed again.
recaps.in_short: In 1968 Claire Randall returns to Inverness with her daughter Brianna and, helped by the young historian Roger Wakefield, finally tells the story of the two years she has never explained. In 1744 she and Jamie Fraser were living in Paris, working to bankrupt and discredit Charles Stuart before he could launch the Jacobite rising they knew would end in slaughter. Their schemes cost them their first child, a daughter born dead after Claire ran to stop a duel, and cost Jamie months in the Bastille. The rising came anyway, and they returned to Scotland and rode out with it, winning at Prestonpans and then watching the army starve and retreat through an English winter. On the eve of Culloden, with the cause lost, Jamie killed Dougal MacKenzie to protect Claire, then sent her back through the standing stones carrying their second child while he went to die with his men. Claire returned to 1948 and to Frank, who raised Brianna as his own. Twenty years on, Roger finds proof that Jamie did not die at Culloden.

recaps.text: Previously, in Outlander: in 1945 Claire Randall, a former army nurse on a second honeymoon in the Scottish Highlands with her historian husband Frank, walked into the ring of standing stones at Craigh na Dun and woke in 1743. Taken up by clansmen of the MacKenzies and suspected of being an English spy, she survived on her medical skill and was compelled to marry a young outlawed Highlander, James Fraser, to put her beyond the reach of the officer hunting her, Captain Jonathan Randall, who was both a sadist and Frank's own direct ancestor. The forced marriage became a real one. Offered the chance to go back through the stones, Claire chose to stay. Jamie was later condemned to hang and brutally abused by Randall at Wentworth Prison; Claire and Jamie's kinsmen broke him out, and Randall was believed to have been killed under a stampede of cattle during the escape. She nursed Jamie back from despair at a French abbey. Knowing from Frank's history that the Jacobite rising of 1745 would end in the destruction of the Highlands at Culloden, the two resolved to stay in France and stop the rising before it could begin. Claire was carrying Jamie's child.

In 1968 Claire Randall comes back to Inverness with her twenty-year-old daughter, Brianna, two years after the death of her husband Frank. They arrive as the household of the late Reverend Reginald Wakefield is being dismantled, and Claire asks the Reverend's adopted son, Roger Wakefield, a young Oxford historian, to find out what became of a company of Highland men who followed one James Fraser in the rising of 1745. Sorting his guardian's papers, Roger comes across the old newspaper reports of Claire's disappearance in 1945 and her reappearance three years later, and cannot make the pieces fit. Claire goes alone to Culloden Moor and stands at the clan stones. Afterwards she tells Roger the truth: she travelled two hundred years through the standing stones at Craigh na Dun, spent those missing years in the eighteenth century, and Brianna is Jamie Fraser's daughter. With Brianna listening, Claire begins the account of what happened after she and Jamie fled Scotland for France, and of how she came to be sent back alone.

The story returns to 1744. Jamie and Claire land in France, where his cousin Jared, a wealthy Paris wine merchant, leaves them his house and his business. Their plan is to stop the Jacobite rising at its source by ruining Charles Stuart's credit and drying up the money and promises that would let him sail for Scotland. Claire is pregnant and increasingly conspicuous in Paris society, which is exactly the position they need. At the docks she recognises smallpox aboard a ship belonging to a French nobleman, the Comte St. Germain, and the vessel and its cargo are destroyed, making them a powerful and unforgiving enemy. Jamie takes a small pickpocket, Fergus, out of a brothel and sets him to stealing the prince's correspondence, while Murtagh watches over the household. Charles himself proves charming, devout, chronically short of funds, and entirely deaf to caution, and Jamie finds that undermining him means lying steadily to men whose cause he was raised to honour.

Claire takes up unpaid work at L'Hopital des Anges, a charity hospital run by the redoubtable Mother Hildegarde, where her skill is welcome and her sex is not remarked on; she also becomes a regular at the crowded shop of an odd apothecary, Master Raymond, who knows more about her than she can account for. At Versailles the couple move among courtiers, mistresses and financiers, and Claire meets Mary Hawkins, a frightened English girl of fifteen being married off to an elderly French nobleman, whose surname Claire recognises from Frank's family tree. Then she meets Alexander Randall, a consumptive young secretary in an English duke's service, and learns from him that his brother Jonathan did not die at Wentworth after all. Jamie's reaction is immediate and murderous. Claire, who knows that the man must live long enough for a particular marriage to take place or Frank will never be born, extracts from Jamie a promise to delay any challenge for a year.

Claire and Mary Hawkins are attacked in the street by masked men; Mary is raped, and the assault is never satisfactorily explained, though the Comte St. Germain's circle is suspected. The promise Claire extracted from Jamie collapses when Jonathan Randall assaults Fergus, and Jamie challenges him to a duel in the Bois de Boulogne. Claire, heavily pregnant, races to stop it, arriving in time to see Jamie wound but not kill his enemy. The strain brings on a haemorrhage. She is carried to L'Hopital des Anges, where her daughter is born dead and Claire herself nearly dies of childbed fever. Jamie, who fought a duel in defiance of a royal edict, is arrested and imprisoned in the Bastille.

Claire names the dead child Faith and is brought back from the edge by Master Raymond, who reaches her in the hospital and does something for her that medicine cannot explain. Grief and blame stand between her and Jamie once he can be reached. To free him, Claire goes to the King, who first requires her presence at a private ordeal in which Master Raymond and the Comte St. Germain are tried for sorcery; the Comte drinks from a poisoned cup and dies. The King then names his own price for Jamie's pardon, and Claire pays it. Jamie is released and banished from France. The two of them, still raw with each other, begin the slow work of repairing what the year has cost, and take ship for Scotland with Fergus and Murtagh.

Jamie's pardon lets him return to Lallybroch, the estate he has not seen in years, where his sister Jenny, her husband Ian and their children have kept the place going. For a time there is something like peace: Jamie farms, Fergus is absorbed into the household, and he and Claire slowly find each other again. It does not last. Charles Stuart, unable to get Jamie's support honestly, publishes a bond of association with Jamie's name forged among the signatures, which makes him a traitor to the Crown whether he joins the rising or not. With no way to stand clear, Jamie decides that the only remaining course is to go out with the Jacobites and try to steer the rising away from the catastrophe Claire knows is coming. Charles lands in Scotland, the clans begin to gather, and Jamie raises men from Lallybroch on the condition that Ian stays behind to hold it.

The rising begins in earnest. Dougal MacKenzie rides in with his men, exultant at the war he has waited his life for, and Jamie takes a place among the prince's officers. At Prestonpans the Highland charge shatters a government army in minutes, and Claire, running a rough field hospital, learns what a victory costs in practice. Edinburgh falls to the Jacobites and Charles holds court there, surrounded by advisers who tell him what he wishes to hear and increasingly deaf to Jamie's warnings about supply, money and the government troops massing in England. Colum MacKenzie, laird of the MacKenzies and dying of his long illness, makes the journey to the prince's camp, settles the succession of his clan, and dies. The army marches south into England, expecting an English rising that never comes.

At Derby the Jacobite commanders turn back, and the long retreat north begins in winter, through snow and hunger, with the government army closing behind. Claire treats frostbite, fever and wounds with almost nothing to work with, and Jamie watches the men of Lallybroch waste away for a prince who will not listen. Sheltering with Mary Hawkins at the house of the Duke of Sandringham, Claire discovers that their genial host has been playing both sides and means to sell them; Murtagh arrives and kills him. In Edinburgh, Alexander Randall is dying of consumption, and Mary is carrying his child. At his brother's request, Jonathan Randall marries Mary so that the child will have a name and a legitimate place, which is the marriage Claire has known all along must happen if Frank is ever to be born. Alex dies, and the ragged army stumbles on toward the moor at Culloden.

On the eve of the battle, with the army starving and the cause plainly lost, Jamie and Claire agree that the only way left to stop the slaughter is to poison Charles Stuart. Dougal MacKenzie overhears them, turns on Claire as a witch and a traitor, and in the struggle Jamie kills him. There is no longer any time. Jamie signs a deed making Lallybroch over to his nephew so the estate cannot be forfeited, sends Murtagh to secure it, and rides with Claire to Craigh na Dun. She is pregnant again. He tells her he means to get the Lallybroch men off the field and then die in the fighting, and asks her to name the child for his father. Claire passes through the stones, returns to 1948, and goes back to Frank, who agrees to raise the child as his own on the condition that she never look for Jamie again. In 1968 the frame closes: Roger's search of the records turns up evidence that James Fraser was not killed at Culloden. Claire, Brianna and Roger are left holding the fact that he lived.

characters.description: Weyrleader of Benden Weyr, bronze rider of Mnementh, and the man who forced Pern to prepare for Thread when nobody believed it was coming. Seven Turns into the Pass he spends as much effort holding Pern's seven Weyrs together as he does fighting Thread: the riders brought forward from four hundred Turns in the past expect an obedience the modern holds and crafts will not give. Impatient with tradition for its own sake, he encourages the crafts to invent and argues that Thread should be stopped at its source rather than burned out of the air twice a week for fifty Turns.
characters.name: F'lar

characters.description: Weyrwoman of Benden and rider of the queen Ramoth, the senior queen of Pern. Born the heir of Ruatha Hold and raised in hiding as a drudge, she is the one who found the five lost Weyrs and brought them forward through time, and she is not allowed to forget either fact. Quick-tempered, possessive of her Weyr and of F'lar, and better than anyone at reading the Records, she is also uneasy about what her rescue of the past has cost the present.
characters.name: Lessa

characters.description: Brown rider of Canth, F'lar's half-brother and wingsecond, and the Weyr's most reliable pair of hands away from Benden. Recovering from a bad Threadscore, he is grounded from fighting for a while, which leaves him time to notice things the busier riders do not.
characters.name: F'nor

characters.description: The Masterharper of Pern, whose craft's teaching songs reach every hold and whose informal network of harpers makes him the best-informed man alive. He supports Benden openly, works to keep the Lord Holders from splitting with the Weyrs, and is one of the few people who can say uncomfortable things to F'lar and be listened to.
characters.name: Robinton

characters.description: The Mastersmith of Pern, an enormous, deliberate man with an obsession with efficiency. His hall has already improved the flamethrowers the ground crews use against Thread, and he is pushing for better ways to send messages across a continent and for instruments the old Records only hint at. His willingness to build new things is exactly what the transplanted riders find offensive.
characters.name: Fandarel

characters.description: A smith of Fandarel's craft, short-sighted, unassertive and gifted with numbers and lenses. Given an ancient instrument nobody has understood for centuries, he sets about working out what it does and what it can be pointed at.
characters.name: Wansor

characters.description: Weyrleader of Fort Weyr and the senior of the riders Lessa brought forward from four hundred Turns in Pern's past. In his own time the Weyrs were served without question by holds and crafts alike, and he sees the modern arrangement as a decline that Benden encourages. Proud, capable in the air and increasingly unwilling to take direction from a younger Weyrleader.
characters.name: T'ron

characters.description: Weyrwoman of Fort Weyr and T'ron's partner, brought forward with him from the past. She expects the deference her rank commanded in her own time and is openly scornful of Benden's Weyrwoman and of the modern crafts.
characters.name: Mardra

characters.description: A young queen rider at Southern Weyr, rider of Wirenth. Raised in a herding hold and trained as a healer of dragons and people, she is conscientious, self-effacing and does most of the Weyr's real work while its senior Weyrwoman is elsewhere. She has fostered several orphaned children of the Weyr and dislikes the arrangements custom makes for queen riders.
characters.name: Brekke

characters.description: Senior Weyrwoman of Southern Weyr, rider of the queen Prideth. Handsome, self-absorbed and interested in her rank chiefly for what it can get her, she spends much of her time away from the Weyr in the company of Lord Holders and leaves the running of Southern to others. Her neglect extends to her own dragon.
characters.name: Kylara

characters.description: A quick, sharp-tongued girl fostered by Brekke at Southern Weyr, orphaned young and anxious to be useful. She is competent well beyond her years at the Weyr's practical work and blunt about what she thinks of the people around her.
characters.name: Mirrim

characters.description: The boy Lord Holder of Ruatha, orphaned at birth and holding the title since infancy, though his warder governs in his name until he comes of age. Curious, chafing at supervision and fascinated by the Weyrs.
characters.name: Jaxom

characters.description: Lord Warder of Ruatha, governing the hold on Jaxom's behalf and raising the boy. A former dragonrider whose dragon died, he carries that loss permanently and holds himself apart because of it; he is scrupulous about Jaxom's inheritance and severe about his education.
characters.name: Lytol

characters.description: Lord Holder of Nabol, who took the hold after the conqueror Fax's death. Ambitious, spiteful and resentful of Benden, he cultivates whatever raises his standing and obstructs whatever does not. He is one of the Lord Holders most willing to deal with the transplanted riders against Benden's interests.
characters.name: Meron

characters.description: A young bronze rider trained at Benden, one of the riders F'lar has been quietly bringing on. He is comfortable with craftsmen and holders, interested in what the smiths are building, and trusted with errands that need discretion rather than rank.
characters.name: N'ton

characters.description: A dragon hatched from an undersized egg on Benden's sands: tiny, white, and unlike anything in the Records. He should not have survived the shell and is not expected to grow, fly properly or ever mate, but he is alert, affectionate and entirely certain of the boy who opened his egg.
characters.name: Ruth

recaps.ending: F'lar defeats T'ron in a knife duel in front of an audience of Lord Holders, craftmasters and riders and, badly wounded, uses the victory to settle the Oldtimer question: the riders who cannot accept the modern world are exiled to the Southern Continent, and the affected Weyrs pass to leaders willing to work with the holds and crafts, among them the young bronze rider N'ton. The search for a permanent answer to Thread produces two results. F'nor and Canth reach the Red Star and find conditions no living thing can survive, closing off any dragon-borne attack for good. Against that, the grubs of the Southern Continent are shown to consume Thread where it burrows, which suggests Pern's ancestors designed a defence in two parts and that the dragons were only the visible half. At a Benden Hatching, Jaxom, the boy Lord Holder of Ruatha, opens an undersized egg with his own hands and Impresses the white dragon Ruth, a pairing that satisfies neither the holds nor the Weyrs and that nobody knows how to undo. Brekke, not chosen by the new queen, accepts that she will never ride again and begins to recover with F'nor. Fire lizards are spreading everywhere, the Pass goes on, and the exiled riders sit in the south unreconciled.
recaps.in_short: Seven Turns after the five lost Weyrs were brought forward through time, Pern is fighting Thread successfully but coming apart socially: the transplanted Oldtimer riders expect an obedience the modern holds and crafts will not give. F'lar of Benden pushes for craft invention and for attacking Thread at its source. F'nor finds a clutch of fire-lizard eggs in the south, and the small telepathic dragon-cousins spread rapidly across Pern. Kylara's neglect of her queen leads to a mating flight in which two queens fight and both die, leaving Brekke dragonless and Kylara destroyed. F'nor's attempt to fly a dragon to the Red Star nearly kills him and ends that hope, but the discovery that Southern's grubs devour Thread in the soil offers a lasting defence. When the Oldtimer leader T'ron challenges F'lar to a knife duel and loses, the irreconcilable riders are exiled to the Southern Continent. At a Benden Hatching, the boy Lord Holder Jaxom helps a tiny white dragon out of its shell and Impresses him.

recaps.text: Pern is periodically scoured by Thread, a spore that falls from a wandering neighbouring planet and devours anything living it touches. The defence is dragons, telepathically bonded for life to their riders, flying from mountain Weyrs and flaming Thread out of the air. In Dragonflight, after four hundred Turns without a Fall, only Benden Weyr was still occupied, and the holds treated the riders as parasites. The bronze rider F'lar, convinced from the Records that Thread was returning, found Lessa, the last heir of Ruatha Hold, hiding as a drudge under the conqueror Fax; he killed Fax, she Impressed the queen Ramoth, and when Ramoth rose to mate F'lar became Weyrleader of Benden. Thread fell as he had predicted, and Benden's two hundred dragons could not cover a planet. After the riders rediscovered that dragons can travel between times as well as between places, Lessa reasoned from an old riddle-song that Pern's five abandoned Weyrs had gone forward in time, rode Ramoth four hundred Turns into the past, and persuaded them to come. They arrived at Benden as an army large enough to defend all of Pern. Pern was saved, but it now holds thousands of riders raised four centuries earlier, who expect a deference the modern holds and crafts no longer wish to give.

Seven Turns have passed since the five Weyrs came forward. The Pass is being fought competently, but the alliance that fights it is fraying. The transplanted riders, called Oldtimers, were raised in a Pern where holds and crafts obeyed the Weyrs without argument, and they resent modern holders who bargain, craftsmen who invent and a young Benden Weyrleader who tells them what to do. F'lar, still Benden's Weyrleader with Lessa as Weyrwoman, is trying to hold seven Weyrs together while pressing two ideas the Oldtimers detest: that the crafts should be encouraged to build new things, and that Thread should be attacked at its source instead of merely burned out of the air every few days for fifty Turns. Mastersmith Fandarel is producing better flamethrowers and pushing for a faster way to send messages across Pern, and the smith Wansor has been handed an ancient instrument nobody has understood in centuries. F'nor, convalescing from a Threadscore at Southern Weyr on the far continent, comes across something no Record mentions: a clutch of fire-lizard eggs on a beach. Fire lizards are small wild cousins of dragons, and they can be Impressed by people in exactly the same way.

The fire lizards change Pern quickly. Eggs are gathered and given out, and the creatures prove affectionate, telepathic within a short range, and able to carry small objects and simple messages. Brekke, the young queen rider who does the real work of Southern Weyr, Impresses one; so does Mirrim, the girl she fosters, who manages three at once, which nobody thought possible. Eggs also reach hands Benden would rather they had not, most notably Lord Meron of Nabol, a spiteful and ambitious holder who is glad of anything that raises his standing and who has been keeping company with Kylara, Southern's senior Weyrwoman. Kylara treats her rank as a privilege and her queen Prideth as an inconvenience, spending her time away from the Weyr. Brekke and F'nor grow close, although custom has other plans for a queen rider. In the north, Fandarel and Wansor turn the ancient instrument out at the sky, and discover it is a distance-viewer that can be pointed at the wandering planet itself.

Brekke's queen Wirenth comes to her first mating flight. Prideth, unattended and beyond Kylara's control, rises at the same time, and the two queens meet in the air. Queens are not supposed to fight; these do, and both die. Brekke is left alive with her dragon dead, a loss riders almost never survive, and she withdraws so completely that F'nor, Manora and her fire lizard are all that keep her breathing. Kylara, whose neglect caused it, breaks entirely and is beyond recovery. The disaster is public, and it hands the Oldtimers exactly the argument they wanted: this, they say, is what modern laxity produces. It also leaves Southern Weyr effectively leaderless and the northern Weyrs badly shaken, at the moment F'lar most needs the seven Weyrs to act as one.

F'lar's argument that Thread should be stopped at its source becomes urgent, and Wansor's work with the distance-viewer gives it substance: the wandering planet can be observed, its orbit calculated and its surface glimpsed. F'nor, grieving and impatient, takes Canth and attempts the flight to the Red Star itself. They reach it and find conditions no living thing can endure, and only just get back; both are badly hurt, and the idea of carrying the fight to the source on dragonback is finished. Almost at the same time the Southern Continent yields a different kind of answer. The soil there is full of grubs that consume Thread where it burrows, protecting the vegetation from below, and the evidence suggests they were deliberately bred by Pern's ancestors as the other half of a defence in which dragons were only the aerial part. If the grubs can be established in the north, Pern's dependence on dragons need not be permanent, which is a conclusion the Oldtimers find intolerable.

The quarrel with the Oldtimers comes to a head in public. With Lord Holders, craftmasters and riders all present, T'ron of Fort Weyr challenges F'lar's authority outright, and the two men fight with belt knives. F'lar wins, badly wounded, and instead of killing his opponent imposes a settlement: the riders who cannot live in the modern world are exiled to the Southern Continent, away from the Weyrs still fighting the Pass, and are to stay there. Fort and the other affected Weyrs pass to leaders willing to work with the holds and crafts, and the younger bronze rider N'ton comes to prominence among them. The split ends the immediate crisis and creates a lasting one: a body of resentful, displaced riders is now settled in the south with nothing left to lose and no Thread of their own to fight.

With the Oldtimer split settled and F'lar recovering from his wounds, Benden holds a Hatching. Among the guests is Jaxom, the boy Lord Holder of Ruatha, brought by his warder Lytol. One egg on the sands is unusually small and the hatchling inside cannot break out of it; Jaxom, standing close enough to reach, opens the shell himself. The dragon that emerges is tiny and white, unlike any dragon in the Records, and it Impresses him on the spot. A Lord Holder is not supposed to be a dragonrider, and a dragon that small is not expected to survive, let alone fly or mate, but Ruth is alive and Jaxom will not give him up. Brekke, brought to the Hatching in the hope that the new queen might choose her, is not chosen and will never ride again, but she begins to come back to herself and to F'nor. Pern closes the book with its Pass being fought, its Oldtimer problem exported rather than solved, the grubs offering a defence that could outlast the dragons, fire lizards spreading everywhere, and a white dragon nobody knows what to do with.

characters.description: A ruler opposing Asshai who awakens after a severe poisoning. He accepts Frisha and Tieran's relationship and remains intent on protecting his people despite the unidentified attack.
characters.name: Rezkin

characters.description: Rezkin's former intended partner, now openly involved with Tieran. She helps manage the crisis around Rezkin's poisoning and the appearance of two identical companions.
characters.name: Frisha

characters.description: Frisha’s partner, who intends to marry her if she agrees. Rezkin accepts their relationship without resentment and wants both of them protected.
characters.name: Tieran Nirius

characters.description: Rezkin's chosen king's mage, though still formally a journeyman. He seeks full standing and proposes entering Asshai to persuade former mage allies to abandon King Caydean.
characters.name: Wesson

characters.description: Rezkin's captive friend and trainee. His location and condition are unknown, and Rezkin is determined to retrieve him personally despite having only just recovered from poisoning.
characters.name: Tamarin Blackwater

characters.description: Tam's fellow quarry slave, bound to him by an enchanted neck-chain. He survives attacks beside Tam and questions whether the quarry stone truly acts under Tam's claimed protection.
characters.name: Uthe

characters.description: Rezkin's trusted striker and security leader. He is already known as a close protector before this volume begins.
characters.name: Kai

characters.description: Rezkin's former trainer and a wary protector who keeps watch throughout the poisoning. He identifies himself as a striker even though Rezkin expects that he may eventually try to kill him.
characters.name: Farson

characters.description: A healer allied with Rezkin who prepares to join the expedition seeking Tam. Her skills make her part of the small party assembled for the rescue.
characters.name: Reaylin de Voss

characters.description: Reaylin's father and the leader of the Asshaian rebels near Benbrick. With Caydean's army due within a day, he asks Wesson to unite the local mages behind the defense.
characters.name: Peyton DeVos

characters.description: The missing prince of Asshai, whose absence is part of the unresolved succession conflict at the start of the volume.
characters.name: Prince Thresson

characters.description: The king of Asshai and an established threat to Rezkin's people. Opposition to his rule shapes the conflict already under way when this volume begins.
characters.name: King Caydean

characters.description: Wesson's former master. He publicly supports Wesson's judgment and ability when the gathered mages of Benbrick must choose their leader before the royal attack.
characters.name: Equestrius

characters.description: A journeyman and natural battle mage among the gathered mages at Benbrick. She joins Wesson with most of the local faction, although her brother remains with the opposing royal force.
characters.name: Alantra Doon

characters.description: A battle mage with an opposing royal force. Alantra Doon’s brother remains aligned with him.
characters.name: Battle Master Rhone

characters.description: An Asshaian operative reported to be directing the siege of Gage. His force seeks a weapon inside the city while mages prepare marked vessels under his control.
characters.name: the Sen

characters.description: The local authority assigned to observe Rezkin while a hidden council assesses whether his power makes him dangerous. He becomes Rezkin's custodian and explains the history of human-born spiritua.
characters.name: the spirit leader

characters.description: A hidden people’s military commander who regards Rezkin with suspicion. She believes his lack of strength could postpone the madness expected of him.
characters.name: the spirit general

characters.description: The wolf-shifting daughter of the leopard leaders. Rezkin saves her from lethal venom, accidentally creating a bond that he alters so she can live independently and regard him as a friend.
characters.name: the bonded wolf-shifter

characters.description: An ancient pointed-eared person who permanently chose a wolf's form. He agrees to oppose the demons and directs Rezkin's party toward the lion tribe and the missing elder they seek.
characters.name: the great wolf

characters.description: An ancient pointed-eared figure leading the lion tribe. He admits murdering lion children born in other forms and blaming rival tribes to manufacture a war, after which his own people take him into custody.
characters.name: the captive lion leader

recaps.ending: At Garton Knoll, the rebels defeat King Caydean's two contingents after Wesson kills Battle Master Rhone and the Sen is removed from the fighting. The Sen escapes the collapsed ruins after opening a pathway. Caydean comes through that passage, but Rezkin forces him back into it before the device collapses. The surge of pathway energy and demonic force leaves Rezkin motionless, and the spirit leader declares him dead. Farson chooses to bury him at Garton Knoll, while Tieran assumes the title of emperor. Tam is alive and travelling with the freed quarry prisoners toward Kyle and his new eastern command in Gendishen. Wesson, Kai, Farson, Reaylin, the spirit companions, and the bonded wolf-shifter survive the battle. Frisha and Prince Thresson remain together in an unknown rune-protected prison. Caydean's destination is unknown, and the missing Sen may possess knowledge capable of restoring Rezkin, leaving Rezkin's death uncertain. The demon threat, pathway technology, fragile alliance of shifting tribes, and danger attached to spiritua power all remain active concerns.
recaps.in_short: After surviving an attempted poisoning, Rezkin accepts Gendishen's crown and sets out to recover Tam. Hidden spirit people identify him as a human-born spiritua whose growing power may eventually drive him mad. He rescues Tam from an Asshaian quarry, heals his damaged mind, and appoints him to command Gendishen's eastern forces. Frisha is secretly kidnapped and replaced by a clay double, then imprisoned with Prince Thresson. Wesson survives the fall of the Asshaian mage academy, unites the mages at Benbrick, and learns that he was fused with a demon before birth. Rezkin builds support among animal-shifting tribes and joins the rebels at Garton Knoll. Wesson kills Battle Master Rhone, while Rezkin wounds the Sen and forces King Caydean through a magical pathway. Its collapse leaves Rezkin motionless and declared dead. The rebels win and Tieran becomes emperor, but Caydean and the Sen remain at large, Frisha and Thresson remain captive, and the possibility of restoring Rezkin is unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Rezkin has become a ruler and the central opponent of King Caydean of Asshai. His allies include Frisha, Tieran Nirius, the strikers Kai and Farson, the journeyman mage Wesson, and his close friend Tam. Prince Thresson remains missing amid the struggle over Asshai's succession. Rezkin's actions have unsettled several kingdoms, and his earlier bargains with ancient beings carry obligations that are not yet fully understood. The conflict has also drawn in demons and unusual magic. As this volume begins, Caydean remains a threat, Tam is absent, and Rezkin's companions are divided among several urgent missions.

Rezkin awakens after a week-long poisoning, but the attacker and toxin remain unknown. He accepts that Frisha and Tieran are now together. Two identical versions of a companion are determined to be equally real people, and Rezkin frees them with different wrist marks. Tam is enslaved in a quarry, chained to another prisoner and suffering from a worsening magical injury to his mind. Rezkin nevertheless acquires a new responsibility when Gendishen's delegates offer him their crown. He accepts, survives an attack during the signing, and gives Wesson a future mandate to end the kingdom's persecution of mages. Wesson plans to seek support within Asshai. Rezkin then leaves to rescue Tam, but two powerful point-eared strangers seize him and his mage companion. They take both through a hostile magical passage to a hidden forest, identify Rezkin's power as spiritua, and warn that the stone he carries suppresses him and may kill him. The rescue is now delayed while Rezkin remains in their custody.

The hidden people determine that Rezkin is a human-born spiritua with access to the full range of their power. They warn that people like him have historically become violently mad, while his emotional suppression has limited both his abilities and that danger. His pendant drains his strength, and his earlier bargain may obligate the hidden people themselves to participate in the coming demon war. The council finds Rezkin sane for the present but assigns the spirit leader to train and monitor him, with authority to kill him if madness appears. The spirit general joins them as pathmaker despite distrusting him. Meanwhile, Tam remains chained in the quarry and is injured in repeated attacks. Stone-bodied ancient beings bound by Rezkin's bargain protect him and offer an escape route. Tam delays leaving because he intends to organize the enslaved workers, and the apparent intervention of the stone begins attracting followers. Conflicting reports place him either on the Isle of Sand or in southern Veril, so Rezkin sends Reaylin toward the island and travels with his new companions toward Veril.

Rezkin's party survives a dragon attack and avalanche while crossing the mountains. His inability to heal the wounded spirit leader exposes how strongly his emotional training constrains spiritua magic. The group learns that a long-missing elder may know how to prevent Rezkin's eventual madness. The spirit leader also identifies Wesson as a human and demon joined in one being, though Rezkin refuses to act against him on that assessment alone. Elsewhere, Wesson continues toward Asshai's mage academies and sinks one pursuing ship and cripples two others with a large-scale attack, leaving him deeply troubled by the deaths. Rezkin detours to besieged Gage after learning that quarry captives may include Tam. He breaks the siege leadership, frees a juvenile dragon intended for demon possession, and leaves the Sen behind at large. At the same time, Frisha is abducted. Her captors create a clay double with her appearance and voice, instruct it to remain near Tieran and Rezkin, and send the real Frisha away in captivity. Her allies do not yet know that the substitution occurred.

Tam's apparent protection by the quarry stone draws nearly thirty prisoners into his escape plan. Rezkin enters the quarry disguised as a new slave, locates Tam and Uthe, and learns that an ancient being has slowed the deterioration of Tam's wounded mind. Concern for Tam gives Rezkin the emotional connection needed to heal him. He closes the injury, frees both men from their enchanted chain, and helps the organized prisoners break out through the mines. With the quarry escape complete, Rezkin offers the survivors a place in Gendishen's forces under Tam. He appoints Tam as eastern general, swordbearer, magistrate, and governor, entrusting him with both authority and a royal blade. Tam remains with the freed prisoners while Rezkin turns toward Asshai. Wesson reaches the mage academy seeking support against Caydean, but its archmage argues for neutrality because the battle-mage academy already supports the king. Her account of Rezkin's rise unsettles Wesson and makes him question whether his loyalty has been manipulated.

Caydean's forces assault the neutral mage academy with battle mages and demon-possessed attackers. Wesson helps evacuate survivors, but the king's adviser kills the archmage and the academy falls. Wesson escapes and heads west toward the rebellion. Rezkin's party, meanwhile, seeks the missing elder who might know how to prevent spiritua madness. They encounter animal-shifting tribes divided by a long war. Rezkin offers valuable supplies needed for shifting in exchange for aid against demons. During the search for the great wolf, he saves the wolf-shifting daughter of the leopard leaders from lethal venom, accidentally forming a dependent bond. He later reshapes it into a non-romantic connection and the two agree to friendship. The great wolf, an ancient pointed-eared person fixed in wolf form, agrees to oppose the demons and leads them to the lion tribe. Its pointed-eared leader admits that he caused the tribal war by murdering children and blaming rival tribes. He is taken into custody, but gives no usable answer to Rezkin's condition. The great wolf and hawk tribe nevertheless bring a wider alliance closer.

Rezkin sends Tam and the former quarry prisoners toward Kyle and Gendishen, then changes course when Wesson reports that a large royal army is approaching Benbrick. Wesson returns to his childhood home, reunites with his mother, and learns that his stepfather serves the rebellion led by Reaylin's father, Peyton DeVos. Frisha awakens in a rune-protected prison and finds Prince Thresson, alive after nearly two years of captivity. At Benbrick, Wesson's former master endorses him, most local mages accept his leadership, and Wesson formally takes mage rank. The spirit people then confirm that Wesson was fused with a demon before birth, when his father diverted the being intended for Caydean. They conclude that Caydean is both demon-possessed and a human-born spiritua. Rezkin joins Peyton's rebels at Garton Knoll without waiting for foreign allies. He intercepts a warning intended for Caydean's army and kills the spies who sent it. He and the spirit general acknowledge mutual feeling, but he withdraws from intimacy. The ambush is prepared against contingents led by Battle Master Rhone and the Sen.

King Caydean visits Frisha and Prince Thresson in prison and reveals that Rezkin is their younger brother. At Garton Knoll, the rebels spring their ambush against royal soldiers, mages, battle mages, and demon-controlled creatures. Wesson isolates Battle Master Rhone and uses his destructive power in a controlled strike to kill him. The Sen opens a magical pathway from the ruins. The bonded wolf-shifter attacks him, but he drains her strength before Rezkin wounds him and the ground collapses. Caydean emerges through the pathway and releases demonic power that overwhelms fighters across the field and blocks Rezkin's own abilities. Rezkin recovers enough control to force Caydean back through the passage, then collapses as the device and demonic energy surge through him. The pathway closes, Caydean's location becomes unknown, and the spirit leader declares Rezkin dead. With Rhone, Caydean, and the Sen gone from the battle, the rebels win and the surviving royal troops retreat. The Sen's body is not found, leaving open the possibility that he escaped and might restore Rezkin. Farson orders Rezkin buried at Garton Knoll, and Tieran becomes emperor while Frisha and Thresson remain captive.

characters.description: A young colonist who arrives on Pern with the Hanrahan family. Curious, adventurous, and unusually receptive to the planet's native creatures, Sorka grows up alongside the settlement and becomes one of the people most closely involved in its transformation.
characters.name: Sorka Hanrahan

characters.description: A boy from the Connell family, whose people bring experience with horses, herding, and a mobile way of life to the colony. Sean is independent, direct, and more comfortable proving himself through action than accepting authority on its own terms.
characters.name: Sean Connell

characters.description: The expedition's admiral and one of the senior leaders responsible for bringing the colonists safely to Pern. Paul supports the settlers' chartered plan for a permanent, largely agrarian society and must balance that ideal with the technical demands of establishing it.
characters.name: Paul Benden

characters.description: The colony's governor and Paul Benden's partner in civil leadership. Emily is calm, diplomatic, and attentive to the different groups that must become a functioning community after the expedition's ships have delivered them.
characters.name: Emily Boll

characters.description: An expert shuttle pilot who helps ferry people and equipment from the colony ships to the surface. Sallah is disciplined, courageous, and committed to the settlement, with the judgment to recognize when a flight requires more than technical skill.
characters.name: Sallah Telgar

characters.description: A talented engineer central to the colony's machinery, power, and transport systems. Tarvi understands that the settlers' decision to limit advanced technology still depends on using their inherited equipment wisely during the dangerous first years.
characters.name: Tarvi Andiyar

characters.description: One of the expedition's most accomplished pilots. Avril values the interstellar skills and technology the colonists intend to leave behind, and she is openly dissatisfied with a future confined to farming on an isolated world.
characters.name: Avril Bitra

characters.description: A senior geneticist whose knowledge is essential to adapting Earth plants and animals to their new environment. Kitti is authoritative, inventive, and prepared to use the colony's biological technology where it offers a durable answer to Pern's needs.
characters.name: Kitti Ping

characters.description: Kitti Ping's granddaughter and scientific assistant. Wind Blossom has inherited formidable technical ability, but she works under the expectations created by her grandmother's reputation and by the colony's urgent biological problems.
characters.name: Wind Blossom

characters.description: Sorka's father, an experienced horseman whose practical knowledge helps establish the colony's herds. Red is protective of his family and willing to judge unfamiliar Pernese life by close observation rather than fear.
characters.name: Red Hanrahan

characters.description: Sorka's mother and a capable member of the colony's farming community. Mairi combines family care with the work of settlement and helps give Sorka the security to explore the new world around Landing.
characters.name: Mairi Hanrahan

characters.description: A geneticist who works with Kitti Ping on the colony's biological program. Pol brings careful scientific knowledge to the adaptation of imported species and to the study of native Pernese life.
characters.name: Pol Nietro

characters.description: A colonist who distrusts the leadership's decisions and objects to the permanence of Pern's isolation. Ted is technically resourceful and persistent, but his determination to appeal beyond the colony places him in conflict with its agreed charter.
characters.name: Ted Tubberman

recaps.ending: The genetically created dragons prove able to bond permanently with human riders, fly, breathe flame after chewing firestone, and travel between places. Sorka and Faranth, Sean and Carenath, and the other first pairs turn Kitti Ping's experiment into a workable defense against Thread. Sean's authority among the riders grows from experience rather than appointment, while Sorka becomes the leading queen rider. The old colony at Landing can no longer remain the center of settlement, so people, animals, and salvageable equipment move north. The dragonriders take the great volcanic caverns above Fort as their home, creating the pattern later known as a Weyr. Avril Bitra's attempt to seize a way off Pern ends in space, and Sallah Telgar dies preventing her escape. The settlers lose much of their connection to advanced interstellar life, but they survive by combining what remains of that knowledge with dragons and new social institutions. Pern's later Holds, Weyrs, and founding legends begin in those choices.
recaps.in_short: Earth colonists arrive on Pern intending to build a permanent low-technology society at Landing. Children Sorka Hanrahan and Sean Connell grow up as the settlement prospers and form bonds with native fire-lizards. Years later, Thread begins falling without warning, consuming living matter and overwhelming the colony's limited aircraft and fuel. Geneticist Kitti Ping enlarges and reshapes fire-lizard embryos to create intelligent defenders. At the first hatching, Sorka bonds with the gold Faranth, Sean with bronze Carenath, and other young people become the first dragonriders. The dragons learn to fly, breathe flame using firestone, and move instantly between locations, giving Pern a renewable defense. Political division and Avril Bitra's attempted escape cost lives, including pilot Sallah Telgar's. Environmental danger and failing technology force the colonists to leave Landing and cross north. Sean, Sorka, and the riders settle in caverns above Fort, establishing the first Weyr and the institutions that will shape Pern after its origins become legend.

recaps.text: Three colony ships reach Pern with settlers who have deliberately chosen a permanent life away from Earth's crowded, technological civilization. Admiral Paul Benden and Governor Emily Boll oversee the descent to Landing, while pilots including Sallah Telgar and Avril Bitra ferry equipment and passengers to the surface. The Hanrahan and Connell families bring horses and practical husbandry alongside scientists, engineers, and farmers. Young Sorka Hanrahan explores eagerly and befriends Sean Connell. Native fire-lizards show unexpected intelligence and an ability to form intense bonds with people, suggesting that Pern's wildlife is stranger and more useful than the initial surveys revealed.

Landing develops into a successful settlement. Crops, herds, and outlying communities spread as the colonists use advanced equipment to establish the simpler society promised by their charter. Sorka and Sean grow toward adulthood, and their connection with fire-lizards deepens their understanding of the creatures' empathy and communication. Not everyone accepts the colony's direction: Avril resents the abandonment of interstellar life, while Ted Tubberman challenges the leadership's authority and looks for help beyond Pern. Even so, most settlers believe the hardest phase is behind them. The records warning of a periodic danger in the system have not yet become part of ordinary colonial planning.

Thread begins falling from the sky, its filaments devouring exposed plants, animals, and people wherever they touch ground. The first attacks devastate unprepared settlements and overturn every assumption about Pern's safety. Aircraft and chemical flamethrowers can destroy Thread in the air, but fuel, machines, and trained crews are finite. Paul, Emily, Tarvi, and the technical teams organize emergency flights and evacuations while trying to understand the Red Star's connection to the falls. The colony can survive individual attacks with its remaining technology, but it needs a defense that can reproduce and endure for generations.

The settlers map Thread's recurring falls and improvise wider defenses, yet every sortie consumes resources they cannot replace. Native fire-lizards can sense Thread and attack it, but they are too small to protect farms and settlements on their own. Kitti Ping proposes using the colony's genetic tools to enlarge and adapt the fire-lizard design into a powerful flying partner for humans. The project is controversial and urgent: the new creatures must remain intelligent and empathic while gaining the size, endurance, and firepower needed to fight Thread. Sorka, Sean, and other young people help tend the altered eggs as the colony waits to learn whether the experiment will produce protectors or another burden.

Kitti Ping's altered eggs hatch into dragons. Each hatchling chooses a human partner in an immediate mental bond: Sorka Impresses the golden Faranth, Sean the bronze Carenath, and the other young attendants form the first group of riders. The dragons grow rapidly, communicate with their riders, and begin learning the coordinated skills their task requires. Sean emerges as a practical leader because he understands both the animals and the independent people bonded to them. The experiment has created a renewable defense in principle, but the inexperienced pairs still have to master flight and discover how dragons can destroy Thread without relying on the colony's dwindling aircraft.

The first dragons and riders learn to fight as a unit. Firestone lets the dragons produce flame, and their ability to move through the cold emptiness called between allows them to cross great distances instantly when given a clear destination. These abilities turn them from a genetic possibility into Pern's best long-term defense. At the same time, the settlement's unity is threatened by people who still hope to recover an interstellar escape. Avril Bitra uses her piloting skills and access to the old ships in pursuit of her own departure, forcing the colony's loyal pilots to act before the remaining orbital resources are taken beyond the settlers' reach.

Avril's attempt to seize a route away from Pern ends in space. Sallah Telgar prevents the theft but dies in the effort, closing off the fantasy that the settlement can simply reverse its founding choice. On the ground, environmental danger and the decline of irreplaceable machinery force a final move away from Landing. The colonists carry north what people, animals, records, and equipment they can save. Sorka and Faranth, Sean and Carenath, and the other dragon pairs have proved they can flame Thread and travel between, so their breeding population can replace the temporary aerial defenses. The riders occupy the vast caverns above the new settlement at Fort, with Sean and Sorka as their central leaders. This first Weyr, together with the developing Holds and crafts, establishes the social order by which later generations will survive the Passes of Thread.

characters.description: A fisherman's daughter from a remote coastal hold, newly brought to the Harper Hall as the Masterharper's own apprentice. She plays every instrument in the hall, writes songs already being sung across Pern, and is bonded to nine fire lizards, the first person known to have Impressed them deliberately. She is also the first girl the Hall has taken as an apprentice, arrives with a badly scarred hand, no craft training, no idea what she is entitled to, and a settled conviction from her upbringing that she is a nuisance who will shortly be sent home.
characters.name: Menolly

characters.description: The Masterharper of Pern, head of a craft whose halls and posted harpers reach every hold on the planet, which makes him both Pern's teacher and its best-informed politician. Genial, hard to mislead and given to arranging things several steps ahead, he brought Menolly to the Hall himself and has not explained to her, or to most of his craftmasters, exactly why.
characters.name: Robinton

characters.description: The gold queen of Menolly's nine fire lizards and the leader of her clutch: small, brilliantly possessive and unwilling to be more than a few feet from her. The other eight take their cue from her, which means Menolly's moods arrive in a room before she does.
characters.name: Beauty

characters.description: Headwoman of the Harper Hall, who runs its kitchens, stores, laundry and lodgings and knows more about its people than any of the craftmasters. Warm and briskly sensible, she is the first person at the Hall to work out that the new apprentice has arrived with nothing and expects less.
characters.name: Silvina

characters.description: A large, simple-minded man who carries and scrubs in the Harper Hall kitchens under Silvina's eye. Slow of speech and easily confused, he is entirely captivated by the fire lizards and becomes devoted to the business of feeding them.
characters.name: Camo

characters.description: The woman who keeps the cottage where the Hall's girl students are lodged. Anxious about her own standing and about the well-connected families whose daughters she houses, she resents having an apprentice, a fisherman's daughter and nine fire lizards imposed on her.
characters.name: Dunca

characters.description: A young apprentice with a celebrated treble voice, an unerring instinct for what is going on anywhere in the Hall, and a habit of trading information for advantage. Cheerful and quite unimpressed by rank, he attaches himself to Menolly early and explains the Hall's politics to her whether or not she asks.
characters.name: Piemur

characters.description: A journeyman harper who works closely with the Masterharper and travels on his errands. Quiet, observant and easy to underestimate, he is one of the few people at the Hall who treats Menolly as a colleague from the start.
characters.name: Sebell

characters.description: The granddaughter of a Lord Holder, lodged in the same cottage as Menolly to be taught the accomplishments expected of a hold's daughter. Conscious of her family's standing and quick to organize the other girls, she takes the arrival of a sea hold's daughter with an apprentice's status as an insult.
characters.name: Pona

characters.description: The Harper Hall's master of composition: exacting, sardonic and openly sceptical that the Masterharper's new apprentice is anything but a fashionable acquisition. He sets Menolly work designed to find the limits of what she can actually do.
characters.name: Domick

characters.description: The Hall's voice master, an enormous man who teaches by bellowing and who cares about nothing except whether a singer is producing the sound properly. He takes Menolly's training in hand without any reference to the argument going on around her.
characters.name: Shonagar

characters.description: The craftmaster in charge of making instruments, absorbed in wood, glue and tuning to the exclusion of Hall politics. He judges people by what their hands produce, which turns out to be a fairer test than Menolly expects.
characters.name: Jerint

characters.description: An elderly craftmaster who teaches musical theory and the strict forms, and who regards the notion of a girl apprenticed to the Harper Craft as an affront to the way things are done. He examines Menolly with the clear intention of finding her wanting.
characters.name: Morshal

characters.description: One of the girls lodged at the cottage, less certain than the rest that the newcomer deserves what is being done to her. She is genuinely interested in music rather than in accomplishments, which puts her at odds with the others.
characters.name: Audiva

characters.description: Masterhealer of Pern, based near the Harper Hall: a small, stooped, extremely capable man who is the first person to look properly at the scar across Menolly's palm and to say what can be done about it. He is blunt about what her family's treatment of the wound cost her.
characters.name: Oldive

characters.description: Lord Holder of Fort Hold, the largest hold on Pern and the Harper Hall's neighbour: loud, choleric, conventional in his views about women and crafts, and determined to have a fire lizard of his own now that he knows they can be Impressed.
characters.name: Lord Groghe

recaps.ending: Menolly's standing at the Harper Hall is settled in her favour on every count. Her hand, treated properly by Masterhealer Oldive and worked steadily, recovers enough for her to play as she used to. The craftmasters who set out to test her, Domick and Morshal in particular, are satisfied by what she can actually do: she sight-reads and performs Domick's demanding new work and holds her own in theory, instrument-making and voice. The trouble at the girls' cottage ends with her out of it and lodged in the Hall itself, and Pona's clique loses its ground. Fire lizards spread further under her instruction, including a queen for Lord Groghe of Fort Hold, and Menolly's own songs are being sung across Pern by harpers who have no idea who wrote them. At the Hall's evening meal the Masterharper ends her apprenticeship after a matter of days and walks her to the journeymen's tables, making her a journeywoman of the Harper Craft, the first woman to hold the rank. Her fear that she was brought to the Hall only as the keeper of nine fire lizards is put to rest: she was brought there to write. What is not settled is what the Masterharper actually intends to do with a journeywoman whose songs travel faster than his harpers do.
recaps.in_short: Menolly arrives at the Harper Hall as the Masterharper's apprentice, the first girl the craft has taken, with nine fire lizards, a scarred hand and no idea what she is entitled to. Lodged among Lord Holders' daughters who resent her, tested by craftmasters who assume she is a fashionable indulgence, and convinced she was brought only because of her fire lizards, she works through a punishing few days of examinations in composition, theory, voice and instrument-making. Master Oldive treats her hand so that it will heal properly; Silvina, the apprentice Piemur, the journeyman Sebell and the kitchen helper Camo take her side; the bullying at the girls' cottage comes to a head and she is moved into the Hall itself.
